translations.literal: [Biography 162: Shi Kefa
translations.idiomatic: [Biography 162: Shi Kefa

sentences.zh: （任民育等·何剛等）〉

translations.literal: (Ren Minyu et al. · He Gang et al.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ren Minyu and others · He Gang and others)〉

sentences.zh: ·高弘圖·薑曰廣

translations.literal: · Gao Hongtu · Jiang Yueguang
translations.idiomatic: · Gao Hongtu · Jiang Yueguang

sentences.zh: （周鑣·雷縯祚）〉】

translations.literal: (Zhou Biao · Lei Yunzuo)〉】〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zhou Biao · Lei Yunzuo)〉】〉

sentences.zh: 史可法，字憲之，大興籍，祥符人。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa, styled Xianzhi, registered in Daxing but a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa, courtesy name Xianzhi, was registered in Daxing but was a native of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 世錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: For generations his family were hundred-household officers in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations as hundred-household officers in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 祖應元舉於鄉，官黃平知州，有惠政。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingyuan passed the provincial examination and served as prefect of Huangping, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingyuan passed the provincial examinations and served as prefect of Huangping, where his policies won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 語其子從質曰：「我家必昌。

translations.literal: He said to his son Congzhi, "Our house is certain to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Congzhi, "Our family is bound to rise.

sentences.zh: 」從質妻尹氏有身，夢文天祥入其舍，生可法。

translations.literal: " When Congzhi's wife, the Lady Yin, was pregnant, she dreamed that Wen Tianxiang entered their dwelling, and Shi Kefa was born.
translations.idiomatic: " While Congzhi's wife Lady Yin was pregnant, she dreamed that Wen Tianxiang entered their home, and thereafter Shi Kefa was born.

sentences.zh: 以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 舉崇禎元年進士，授西安府推官，稍遷戶部主事，曆員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Chongzhen, was appointed push officer of Xi'an Prefecture, and was gradually promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, then served successively as secretary and director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the first year of the Chongzhen reign, was appointed reviewing officer of Xi'an Prefecture, and was gradually promoted through the Ministry of Revenue to supervising secretary, secretary, and director.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷右參議，分守池州、太平。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to right assistant administrator and assigned to defend Chizhou and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to right assistant administrator with responsibility for Chizhou and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 其秋，總理侍郎盧象升大舉討賊。

translations.literal: That autumn, Vice Minister Lu Xiangsheng, as supreme commander, launched a major campaign against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, supreme commander Lu Xiangsheng, in his capacity as vice minister, mounted a major campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 改可法副使，分巡安慶、池州，監江北諸軍。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa was changed to vice commissioner and assigned to patrol Anqing and Chizhou, supervising all armies north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa was reassigned as vice commissioner to patrol Anqing and Chizhou and to supervise all forces north of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 黃梅賊掠宿松、潛山、太湖，將犯安慶，可法追擊之潛山天堂寨。

translations.literal: Bandits from Huangmei raided Susong, Qianshan, and Taihu and were about to invade Anqing; Kefa pursued them to Tiantang Stockade in Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Huangmei plundered Susong, Qianshan, and Taihu and were poised to strike Anqing; Kefa pursued them to Tiantang Stockade in Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 明年，祖寬破賊滁州，賊走河南。

translations.literal: The next year Zu Kuan defeated the bandits at Chuzhou, and the bandits fled to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zu Kuan routed the rebels at Chuzhou, and they fled into Henan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊馬守應合羅汝才、李萬慶自鄖陽東下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandit Ma Shouying joined Luo Rucai and Li Wanqing and marched east from Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebel Ma Shouying united with Luo Rucai and Li Wanqing and marched east from Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 可法馳駐太湖，扼其沖。

translations.literal: Kefa hastened to station himself at Taihu and blocked their line of advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa rushed to Taihu and blocked their path of advance.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，賊從間道突安慶石牌，尋移桐城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year the bandits burst through a bypath into Shipai in Anqing, then soon shifted to Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year the rebels struck Anqing's Shipai by a hidden route, then soon moved on to Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 參將潘可大擊走賊，賊復為廬、風軍所扼，回桐城，掠四境。

translations.literal: Regimental commander Pan Keda drove the bandits off, but they were again checked by the Luzhou and Fengyang forces, returned to Tongcheng, and plundered the surrounding districts.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commander Pan Keda beat the rebels back, but they were checked again by the Luzhou and Fengyang armies, withdrew to Tongcheng, and ravaged the countryside on all sides.

sentences.zh: 知縣陳爾銘嬰城守，可法與可大剿捕。

translations.literal: Magistrate Chen Erming defended the walled city, and Kefa joined Keda in pursuing and suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Chen Erming held the city under siege, while Kefa and Keda led the pursuit and suppression.

sentences.zh: 賊走廬江，犯潛山，可法與左良玉敗之楓香驛，賊乃竄潛山、太湖山中。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Lujiang and invaded Qianshan; Kefa and Zuo Liangyu defeated them at Maple Fragrance Post, and the bandits then hid in the mountains of Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Lujiang and struck at Qianshan; Kefa and Zuo Liangyu defeated them at Maple Fragrance Post, after which they took refuge in the mountains of Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 三月，可大及副將程龍敗歿於宿松。

translations.literal: In the third month Keda and vice commander Cheng Long were defeated and killed at Susong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Keda and vice commander Cheng Long were defeated and killed at Susong.

sentences.zh: 賊分其黨搖天動別為一營，而合八營二十餘萬眾，分屯桐城之練潭、石井、陶沖。

translations.literal: The bandits split off their partisan Yao Tiandong into a separate camp, while the eight camps together mustered more than two hundred thousand men and encamped separately at Liantan, Shijing, and Taochong in Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels detached their partisan Yao Tiandong as a separate camp, while the eight camps together fielded more than two hundred thousand men and encamped at Liantan, Shijing, and Taochong in Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 總兵官牟文綬、劉良佐擊敗之掛車河。

translations.literal: Regional commanders Mou Wenshou and Liu Liangzuo defeated them at Guache River.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders Mou Wenshou and Liu Liangzuo defeated them at Guache River.

sentences.zh: 當是時，陝寇聚漳、寧，分犯岷、洮、秦、楚、應、皖，群盜遍野。

translations.literal: At that time Shaanxi bandits gathered in Zhang and Ning and raided in separate columns into Min, Tao, Qin, Chu, Ying, and Wan; gangs of robbers covered the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shaanxi rebels massed in Zhang and Ning and sent raiding columns into Min, Tao, Qin, Chu, Ying, and Wan, until bandits swarmed across the land.

sentences.zh: 總理盧象升既改督宣、大，代以王家禎，祖寬關外兵亦北歸。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Lu Xiangsheng had already been transferred to govern Xuan and Da; Wang Jiazhen replaced him, and Zu's troops from beyond the passes also returned north.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Lu Xiangsheng had already been reassigned to govern Xuanfu and Datong; Wang Jiazhen replaced him, and Zu's frontier army likewise marched north again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上復以熊文燦代家禎，專撫賊。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor again appointed Xiong Wencan in place of Jiazhen to pacify the bandits exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor again replaced Jiazhen with Xiong Wencan, charging him solely with pacifying the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊益狂逞，盤牙江北，南都震驚。

translations.literal: The bandits grew still more rampant, entrenched themselves north of the Yangtze, and the Southern Capital was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew bolder still, dug in north of the Yangtze, and alarm spread through the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 七月擢可法右僉都御史，巡撫安慶、廬州、太平、池州四府，及河南之光州、光山、固始、羅田，湖廣之蘄州、廣濟、黃梅，江西之德化、湖口諸縣，提督軍務，設額兵萬人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Kefa was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the four prefectures of Anqing, Luzhou, Taiping, and Chizhou, together with Guangzhou, Guangshan, Gushi, and Luotian in Henan; Qizhou, Guangji, and Huangmei in Huguang; and Dehua, Hukou, and other counties in Jiangxi; he was charged with military affairs and given a quota force of ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Kefa was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Anqing, Luzhou, Taiping, and Chizhou, as well as Guangzhou, Guangshan, Gushi, and Luotian in Henan; Qizhou, Guangji, and Huangmei in Huguang; and Dehua, Hukou, and other counties in Jiangxi. He was put in charge of military affairs and allotted a standing force of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賊已東陷和州、含山、定遠、六合，犯天長、盱眙，趨河南。

translations.literal: The bandits had already overrun Hezhou, Hanshan, Dingyuan, and Luhe in the east, attacked Tianchang and Xuyi, and pressed toward Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already seized Hezhou, Hanshan, Dingyuan, and Luhe in the east, struck at Tianchang and Xuyi, and were pressing toward Henan.

sentences.zh: 可法奏免被災田租。

translations.literal: Kefa memorialized for exemption of land tax in disaster-stricken fields.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa memorialized to remit land tax on fields stricken by disaster.

sentences.zh: 冬，部將汪雲鳳敗賊潛山，京軍復連破老回回舒城、廬江，賊遁入山。

translations.literal: In winter his subordinate Wang Yunfeng defeated the bandits at Qianshan; the capital army again defeated Lao Huíhui at Shucheng and Lujiang in succession, and the bandits fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his subordinate Wang Yunfeng defeated the rebels at Qianshan; the capital army in turn routed Lao Huíhui at Shucheng and Lujiang, and the rebels withdrew into the hills.

sentences.zh: 時監軍僉事湯開遠善擊賊，可法東西馳禦，賊稍稍避其鋒。

translations.literal: At the time supervising secretary Tang Kaiyuan was skilled at striking bandits; Kefa rushed east and west to meet them, and the bandits gradually avoided his edge.
translations.idiomatic: At the time supervising secretary Tang Kaiyuan was adept at fighting rebels; Kefa raced back and forth to meet them, and the rebels gradually gave his forces a wide berth.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏，以平賊逾期，戴罪立功。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year, because pacifying the bandits was overdue, he was ordered to redeem his fault by meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eleventh year, because the campaign to pacify the rebels had overrun its deadline, he was ordered to atone by achieving merit in the field.

sentences.zh: 可法短小精悍，面黑，目爍爍有光。

translations.literal: Kefa was short, compact, and vigorous; his face was dark, and his eyes glittered with light.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa was short, wiry, and formidable; his face was dark, and his eyes shone with a keen light.

sentences.zh: 廉信，與下均勞苦。

translations.literal: He was incorrupt and trustworthy, and shared hardship equally with those below him.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and trustworthy, and shared hardship equally with the men under him.

sentences.zh: 軍行，士不飽不先食，未授衣不先禦，以故得士死力。

translations.literal: On campaign he would not eat before his soldiers were fed, nor put on warm clothing before they had been issued theirs; for this reason he won their utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he would not eat until his men were fed, nor take warm clothing until they had been issued theirs; for this reason they gave him their lives willingly.

sentences.zh: 連敗賊英山、六合，順天王乞降。

translations.literal: He defeated the bandits repeatedly at Yingshan and Luhe, and Shuntian Wang begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels repeatedly at Yingshan and Luhe, until Shuntian Wang sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二年夏，丁外艱去。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twelfth year he left office upon the death of his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twelfth year he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起戶部右侍郎兼右僉都御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled as right vice minister of revenue and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was recalled as right vice minister of revenue and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 代硃大典總督漕運，巡撫鳳陽、淮安、揚州，劾罷督糧道三人，增設漕儲道一人，大浚南河，漕政大厘。

translations.literal: He replaced Zhu Dadian as grand coordinator of the grain transport, and as grand coordinator of Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou; he impeached and removed three grain-route commissioners, added one commissioner for transport reserves, greatly dredged the Southern Canal, and greatly reformed transport administration.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Zhu Dadian as director-general of grain transport and as grand coordinator of Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou. He impeached and dismissed three grain-route commissioners, added one commissioner for transport reserves, undertook a major dredging of the Southern Canal, and brought transport administration into good order.

sentences.zh: 拜南京兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of war at Nanjing and assistant in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of war at Nanjing with a role in deliberating military affairs.

sentences.zh: 因武備久弛，奏行更新八事。

translations.literal: Because military preparations had long been neglected, he memorialized to carry out eight measures of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Because military readiness had long been neglected, he memorialized proposing eight measures to restore it.

sentences.zh: 十七年四月朔，聞賊犯闕，誓師勤王。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month of the seventeenth year, hearing that bandits had attacked the capital, he rallied his army to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month of the seventeenth year, upon hearing that rebels had struck the capital, he rallied his troops to march to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 渡江抵浦口，聞北都既陷，縞衣發喪。

translations.literal: He crossed the river and reached Pukou; hearing that the Northern Capital had already fallen, he put on unhemmed white garments and proclaimed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze and reached Pukou; when he learned that the Northern Capital had already fallen, he donned plain white mourning dress and proclaimed the calamity.

sentences.zh: 會南都議立君，張慎言、呂大器、薑曰廣等曰：「福王由崧，神宗孫也，倫序當立，而有七不可：貪、淫、酗酒、不孝、虐下、不讀書、干預有司也。

translations.literal: It happened that the Southern Capital debated enthroning a ruler; Zhang Shenyan, Lü Daqi, Jiang Yueguang, and others said, "Prince Fu Zhu Yousong is a grandson of Emperor Shenzong and by order of succession ought to be enthroned, yet there are seven disqualifications: greed, lewdness, heavy drinking, lack of filial piety, cruelty to subordinates, failure to study, and meddling with officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Southern Capital debated which prince to enthrone. Zhang Shenyan, Lü Daqi, Jiang Yueguang, and others said, "Prince Fu Zhu Yousong is a grandson of Emperor Shenzong and stands first in the order of succession, yet there are seven reasons he should not reign: greed, lewdness, heavy drinking, lack of filial piety, cruelty to subordinates, neglect of learning, and interference with officials.

sentences.zh: 潞王常訁芳，神宗侄也，賢明當立。

translations.literal: Prince Lu Zhu Changfang is a nephew of Emperor Shenzong, worthy and enlightened, and ought to be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu Zhu Changfang is a nephew of Emperor Shenzong, worthy and enlightened, and should be enthroned instead.

sentences.zh: 」移牒可法，可法亦以為然。

translations.literal: " They sent a dispatch to Kefa, and Kefa also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " They sent a dispatch to Kefa, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽總督馬士英潛與阮大鋮計議，主立福王，咨可法，可法以七不可告之。

translations.literal: Fengyang governor-general Ma Shiying secretly plotted with Ruan Dacheng and advocated enthroning Prince Fu; he consulted Kefa, and Kefa told him of the seven disqualifications.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang governor-general Ma Shiying secretly plotted with Ruan Dacheng in favor of enthroning Prince Fu. He consulted Kefa, who repeated the seven disqualifications.

sentences.zh: 而士英已與黃得功、劉良佐、劉澤清、高傑發兵送福王至儀真，於是可法等迎王。

translations.literal: But Shiying had already joined Huang Degong, Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie in dispatching troops to escort Prince Fu to Yizhen; thereupon Kefa and the others went out to welcome the prince.
translations.idiomatic: But Shiying had already joined Huang Degong, Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie in marching troops to escort Prince Fu to Yizhen, and so Kefa and the others went out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，王謁孝陵、奉先殿，出居內守備府。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month the prince visited Xiaoling and the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, then moved out to lodge at the Inner Palace Guard headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month the prince paid his respects at Xiaoling and the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, then took up residence at the Inner Palace Guard headquarters.

sentences.zh: 群臣入朝，王色赧欲避。

translations.literal: When the officials entered audience, the prince flushed and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials came to audience, the prince flushed and shrank back.

sentences.zh: 可法曰：「王毋避，宜正受。

translations.literal: Kefa said, "Your Highness must not withdraw; you should receive them properly.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa said, "Your Highness must not withdraw; you should receive them as is proper.

sentences.zh: 」既朝，議戰守。

translations.literal: " After the audience they debated war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: " After the audience they debated strategy for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 可法曰：「王宜素服郊次，發師北征，示天下以必報仇之義。

translations.literal: Kefa said, "Your Highness ought to wear plain garments and lodge in the suburbs, raise an army for a northern expedition, and show the empire the resolve to take revenge without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa said, "Your Highness ought to wear plain mourning dress and lodge outside the city, raise an army for a northern expedition, and show the empire that vengeance is imperative.

sentences.zh: 」王唯唯。

translations.literal: " The prince assented vaguely.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 明日再朝，出議監國事。

translations.literal: The next day, at a second audience, they withdrew to debate affairs of regency.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at a second audience, they withdrew to discuss the regency.

sentences.zh: 張慎言曰：「國虛無人，可遂即大位。

translations.literal: Zhang Shenyan said, "The state is vacant and without a ruler; Your Highness may at once ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenyan said, "The throne stands empty; Your Highness may ascend it at once.

sentences.zh: 」可法曰：「太子存亡未卜，倘南來若何？

translations.literal: " Kefa said, "Whether the crown prince lives or dies is still unknown; if he should come south, what then?
translations.idiomatic: " Kefa said, "We do not yet know whether the crown prince is alive; if he should come south, what then?

sentences.zh: 」誠意伯劉孔昭曰：「今日既定，誰敢復更？

translations.literal: " Sincerity Earl Liu Kongzhao said, "Once settled today, who would dare change it again?
translations.idiomatic: " Sincerity Earl Liu Kongzhao said, "Once the matter is settled today, who would dare reopen it?

sentences.zh: 」可法曰：「徐之。

translations.literal: " Kefa said, "Let it wait.
translations.idiomatic: " Kefa said, "Let us wait.

sentences.zh: 」乃退。

translations.literal: " Then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又明日，王監國，廷推閣臣，眾舉可法、高弘圖、薑曰廣。

translations.literal: On the following day the prince assumed regency; at court recommendation for grand secretaries the assembly nominated Kefa, Gao Hongtu, and Jiang Yueguang.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day the prince assumed the regency, and at court recommendation for grand secretaries the assembly nominated Kefa, Gao Hongtu, and Jiang Yueguang.

sentences.zh: 孔昭攘臂欲並列，眾以本朝無勳臣入閣例，遏之。

translations.literal: Kongzhao rolled up his sleeves and wished to be ranked with them, but the assembly, citing that this dynasty had no precedent for ennobled ministers entering the Secretariat, checked him.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao rolled up his sleeves and demanded equal standing, but the assembly, citing the lack of precedent for ennobled ministers in the Secretariat, blocked him.

sentences.zh: 孔昭勃然曰：「即我不可，馬士英何不可？

translations.literal: Kongzhao flushed with anger and said, "If I may not, why may Ma Shiying not?
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao flushed with anger and said, "If I may not serve, why may Ma Shiying not?

sentences.zh: 」乃並推士英。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they also nominated Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they nominated Shiying as well.

sentences.zh: 又議起廢，推鄭三俊、劉宗周、徐石麒。

translations.literal: They also debated recalling dismissed officials and nominated Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, and Xu Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: They also debated recalling dismissed officials and nominated Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, and Xu Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 孔昭舉大鋮，可法曰：「先帝欽定逆案，毋復言。

translations.literal: Kongzhao nominated Dacheng; Kefa said, "The late emperor definitively settled the treason case; let it not be raised again.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao nominated Dacheng; Kefa said, "The late emperor definitively settled the treason case; let the matter not be reopened.

sentences.zh: 」越二日，拜可法禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與士英、弘圖並命。

translations.literal: " Two days later Kefa was appointed minister of rites and concurrently grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, together with Shiying and Hongtu.
translations.idiomatic: " Two days later Kefa was appointed minister of rites and concurrently grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, together with Shiying and Hongtu.

sentences.zh: 可法仍掌兵部事，士英仍督師鳳陽。

translations.literal: Kefa still directed the Ministry of War; Shiying still commanded armies at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa continued to direct the Ministry of War, while Shiying continued to command armies at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 乃定京營制，如北都故事，侍衛及錦衣衛諸軍，悉入伍操練。

translations.literal: They then fixed the capital garrison system according to the precedent of the Northern Capital; palace guards and all troops of the Embroidered Uniform Guard were enrolled for drill.
translations.idiomatic: They then reorganized the capital garrison on the model of the Northern Capital, enrolling palace guards and all Embroidered Uniform Guard troops for drill.

sentences.zh: 錦衣東西兩司房，及南北兩鎮撫司官，不備設，以杜告密，安人心。

translations.literal: The eastern and western offices of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the officials of the northern and southern regional commissions were not fully staffed, so as to cut off secret denunciations and reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western offices of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the northern and southern regional commissions were left understaffed, so as to cut off secret denunciations and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 可法去，士英、孔昭輩益無所憚。

translations.literal: When Kefa departed, Shiying, Kongzhao, and their faction grew still less restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kefa was gone, Shiying, Kongzhao, and their allies grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 孔昭以慎言舉吳甡，嘩殿上，拔刀逐慎言。

translations.literal: Kongzhao, because Shenyan had recommended Wu Shen, raised an uproar in the hall, drew his sword, and drove Shenyan out.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shenyan had recommended Wu Shen, Kongzhao raised an uproar in the hall, drew his sword, and drove Shenyan out.

sentences.zh: 可法馳疏解，孔昭卒扼甡不用。

translations.literal: Kefa rushed a memorial to explain, but Kongzhao in the end blocked Shen and he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa rushed in a memorial to explain, but Kongzhao in the end blocked Wu Shen, who was never appointed.

sentences.zh: 可法祭二陵畢，上疏曰：「陛下踐阼初，祗謁孝陵，哭泣盡哀，道路感動。

translations.literal: When Kefa had finished sacrificing at the two mausoleums, he submitted a memorial saying, "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you reverently visited Xiaoling and wept with full grief; travelers on the road were moved.
translations.idiomatic: After Kefa had completed the sacrifices at the two imperial mausoleums, he submitted a memorial saying, "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you reverently visited Xiaoling and wept with full grief, and travelers on the road were moved.

sentences.zh: 若躬謁二陵，親見泗、鳳蒿萊滿目，雞犬無聲，當益悲憤。

translations.literal: If you personally visited the two mausoleums and saw with your own eyes how Sizhou and Fengyang were overgrown to the horizon and silent of fowl and dog, you would feel still greater grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: If you were to visit the two mausoleums in person and see Sizhou and Fengyang overgrown to the horizon, silent of fowl and dog, your grief and indignation would only deepen.

sentences.zh: 願慎終如始，處深宮廣廈，則思東北諸陵魂魄之未安；

translations.literal: I pray you be as careful at the end as at the beginning: when you dwell in deep palaces and broad halls, then think how the souls of the northeastern mausoleums are not yet at rest;
translations.idiomatic: I pray you be as careful at the end as at the beginning: when you dwell in deep palaces and broad halls, remember that the souls of the northeastern mausoleums are not yet at rest;

sentences.zh: 享玉食大庖，則思東北諸陵麥飯之無展；

translations.literal: when you enjoy jade fare and great kitchens, then think how the northeastern mausoleums have not even barley rice set out;
translations.idiomatic: when you enjoy jade fare and great kitchens, remember that the northeastern mausoleums have not even a bowl of barley rice set out;

sentences.zh: 膺圖受籙，則念先帝之集木馭朽，何以忽遘危亡；

translations.literal: when you receive the chart and accept the mandate, then recall how the late emperor gathered kindling while the carriage rotted—how did ruin come so suddenly;
translations.idiomatic: when you receive the chart and accept the mandate, recall how the late emperor gathered kindling while the carriage rotted—how did ruin come upon us so suddenly;

sentences.zh: 早朝晏罷，則念先帝之克儉克勤，何以卒隳大業。

translations.literal: when you attend court early and retire late, then recall how the late emperor was frugal and diligent—how did he in the end destroy the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: when you attend court early and retire late, recall how the late emperor was frugal and diligent—how did he in the end lose the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 戰兢惕厲，無時怠荒，二祖列宗將默佑中興。

translations.literal: Tremble in awe, be vigilant and strenuous, and never at any time grow negligent; the two founders and the line of ancestors will silently aid restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Tremble in awe, be vigilant and strenuous, and never grow negligent; the two founders and the line of ancestors will silently aid our restoration.

sentences.zh: 若晏處東南，不思遠略，賢奸無辨，威斷不靈，老成投簪，豪傑裹足，祖宗怨恫，天命潛移，東南一隅未可保也。

translations.literal: If you dwell at ease in the southeast, give no thought to distant strategy, distinguish neither worthy from villain, wield no decisive authority, drive old statesmen to cast aside their caps and heroes to bind up their feet, then the ancestors will resent and grieve, Heaven's mandate will shift in secret, and even this corner of the southeast cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If you dwell at ease in the southeast, give no thought to distant strategy, distinguish neither the worthy from the villainous, wield no decisive authority, drive old statesmen to resign and heroes to hold back, then the ancestors will resent and grieve, Heaven's mandate will shift in secret, and even this corner of the southeast cannot be preserved.

sentences.zh: 」王嘉答之。

translations.literal: " The prince praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince praised the memorial and replied.

sentences.zh: 得功、澤清、傑爭欲駐揚州。

translations.literal: Degong, Zeqing, and Jie each contended to station themselves at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Degong, Zeqing, and Jie each vied to station their troops at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 傑先至，大殺掠，屍橫野。

translations.literal: Jie arrived first and carried out great slaughter and plunder; corpses lay across the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jie arrived first and carried out widespread slaughter and plunder; corpses lay across the fields.

sentences.zh: 城中恟懼，登陴守，傑攻之浹月。

translations.literal: The city was panic-stricken; they manned the walls in defense, and Jie besieged it for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized the city; the people manned the walls in defense, and Jie besieged it for a full month.

sentences.zh: 澤清亦大掠淮上。

translations.literal: Zeqing also carried out great plunder along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing likewise ravaged the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 臨淮不納良佐軍，亦被攻。

translations.literal: Linhuai refused to admit Liangzuo's army and was also attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Linhuai refused to admit Liangzuo's army and came under attack as well.

sentences.zh: 朝命可法往解，得功、良佐、澤清皆聽命。

translations.literal: The court ordered Kefa to go and mediate; Degong, Liangzuo, and Zeqing all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Kefa to go and mediate; Degong, Liangzuo, and Zeqing all submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 乃詣傑。

translations.literal: Then he went to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to see Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑素憚可法，可法來，傑夜掘坎十百，埋暴骸。

translations.literal: Jie had always feared Kefa; when Kefa came, Jie dug trenches by the hundreds that night and buried the exposed corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had always feared Kefa; when Kefa arrived, Jie spent the night digging hundreds of trenches to bury the exposed corpses.

sentences.zh: 旦日朝可法帳中，辭色俱變，汗浹背。

translations.literal: At dawn he attended at Kefa's headquarters; his words and expression both changed, and sweat soaked his back.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he came to Kefa's headquarters; his manner and expression both changed, and sweat soaked his back.

sentences.zh: 可法坦懷待之，接偏裨以溫語，傑大喜過望。

translations.literal: Kefa received him with open candor and addressed his junior officers with warm words; Jie was delighted beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa received him with open candor and addressed his junior officers with warm words; Jie was delighted beyond his hopes.

sentences.zh: 然傑亦自是易可法，用己甲士防衛，文檄必取視而後行。

translations.literal: Yet from this Jie also took liberties with Kefa, using his own armored soldiers as guards; every dispatch had to be taken and read before it could be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from this Jie also grew bolder toward Kefa, posting his own armored guards around him; every dispatch had to pass through Jie's hands before it could be issued.

sentences.zh: 可法夷然為具疏，屯其眾於瓜洲，傑又大喜。

translations.literal: Kefa remained unmoved, drew up a memorial for him, and stationed his troops at Guazhou; Jie was again greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa remained unmoved, drew up the memorial for him, and stationed his troops at Guazhou; Jie was again greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 傑去，揚州以安，可法乃開府揚州。

translations.literal: When Jie departed, Yangzhou was pacified, and Kefa then opened his headquarters at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie withdrew, Yangzhou was pacified, and Kefa then established his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 六月，大清兵擊敗賊李自成，自成棄京師西走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Great Qing army defeated the bandit Li Zicheng; Zicheng abandoned the capital and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Qing army defeated the rebel Li Zicheng, and Zicheng abandoned the capital and fled west.

sentences.zh: 青州諸郡縣爭殺偽官，據城自保。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties of Qingzhou vied to kill the false officials and held their cities in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Qingzhou, prefectures and counties vied to kill the puppet officials and held their cities in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 可法請頒監國、登極二詔，慰山東、河北軍民心。

translations.literal: Kefa requested the promulgation of two edicts, on the regency and on enthronement, to reassure the hearts of soldiers and civilians in Shandong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa asked that two edicts be issued—one on the regency and one on enthronement—to reassure soldiers and civilians in Shandong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 開禮賢館，招四方才智，以監紀推官應廷吉領其事。

translations.literal: He opened a Hall for Honoring the Worthy, recruited talent from all quarters, and put supervising secretary Ying Tingji in charge.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a Hall for Honoring the Worthy to recruit talent from all quarters, placing supervising secretary Ying Tingji in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 八月出巡淮安，閱澤清士馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he went on inspection to Huai'an and reviewed Zeqing's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he inspected Huai'an and reviewed Zeqing's troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 返揚州，請餉為進取資。

translations.literal: Returning to Yangzhou, he requested funds as resources for an advance.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Yangzhou he requested pay and supplies to fund a northern advance.

sentences.zh: 士英靳不發，可法疏趣之。

translations.literal: Shiying was stingy and would not release them; Kefa memorialized to urge him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was stingy and refused to release the funds; Kefa memorialized to press him.

sentences.zh: 因言：「邇者人才日耗，仕途日淆，由名心勝而實意不修，議論多而成功少。

translations.literal: He also said, "Lately talent is daily exhausted and official careers daily confused, because ambition for reputation prevails while genuine purpose is not cultivated, and talk is abundant while success is scarce.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Lately talent grows scarcer and official careers more corrupt, because men chase reputation rather than cultivate real purpose, and talk is plentiful while achievement is rare.

sentences.zh: 今事勢更非昔比，必專主討賊復仇。

translations.literal: The situation now is nothing like the past; we must devote ourselves solely to punishing the bandits and taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The situation now is nothing like before; we must devote ourselves solely to punishing the rebels and taking revenge.

sentences.zh: 舍籌兵籌餉無議論，舍治兵治餉無人才。

translations.literal: Apart from planning troops and planning pay there should be no discussion; apart from training troops and managing pay there should be no talent employed.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from planning troops and supplies there should be no debate; apart from training troops and managing pay there should be no appointments.

sentences.zh: 有摭拾浮談、巧營華要者，罰無赦！

translations.literal: Whoever gathers idle talk and craftily seeks splendid posts—punish without pardon!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever trades in idle talk and craftily seeks splendid posts—let him be punished without mercy!

sentences.zh: 」王優詔答之。

translations.literal: " The prince answered with an edict of favor.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 初，可法虞傑跋扈，駐得功儀真防之。

translations.literal: Earlier Kefa had feared Jie's arrogance and stationed Degong at Yizhen to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kefa had feared Jie's arrogance and stationed Degong at Yizhen to keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 九月朔，得功、傑構兵，曲在傑。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month Degong and Jie raised troops against each other; the fault lay with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month Degong and Jie clashed; the fault lay with Jie.

sentences.zh: 賴可法調劑，事得解。

translations.literal: Thanks to Kefa's mediation the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Kefa's mediation the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 北都降賊諸臣南還，可法言：「諸臣原籍北土者，宜令赴吏、兵二部錄用，否則恐絕其南歸之心。

translations.literal: The officials of the Northern Capital who had surrendered to the bandits returned south; Kefa said, "Those whose native places are in the north ought to be ordered to present themselves to the Ministries of Personnel and War for appointment; otherwise we may cut off their desire to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Northern Capital who had surrendered to the rebels were returning south. Kefa said, "Those whose native places lie in the north should be ordered to present themselves to the Ministries of Personnel and War for appointment; otherwise we may destroy their wish to come south.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「北都之變，凡屬臣子皆有罪。

translations.literal: " He also said, "In the calamity of the Northern Capital, every subject was guilty.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "In the fall of the Northern Capital, every subject bore guilt.

sentences.zh: 在北者應從死，豈在南者非人臣？

translations.literal: Those in the north ought to have followed their ruler in death—are those in the south not subjects?
translations.idiomatic: Those in the north ought to have died with their ruler—are those in the south any less his subjects?

sentences.zh: 即臣可法謬典南樞，臣士英叨任鳳督，未能悉東南甲疾趨北援，鎮臣澤清、傑以兵力不支，折而南走。

translations.literal: Even I, Kefa, wrongly held the southern command, and Shiying presumptuously held the Fengyang post; we failed to muster all the armor of the southeast and hurry north in aid. The regional commanders Zeqing and Jie, their forces insufficient, turned and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Even I, Kefa, wrongly held the southern command, and Shiying presumptuously held the Fengyang post; we failed to muster the armies of the southeast and hurry north. Regional commanders Zeqing and Jie, their forces insufficient, turned south instead.

sentences.zh: 是首應重論者，臣等罪也。

translations.literal: We are the ones who ought first to be heavily judged; this is our crime.
translations.idiomatic: We are the ones who ought first to be judged severely; the guilt is ours.

sentences.zh: 乃因聖明繼統，钅未鉞未加，恩榮疊被。

translations.literal: Yet because the sage ruler succeeded to the throne, the axe and halberd were not applied, and favor and honor were heaped upon us.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the sage ruler succeeded to the throne, no punishment fell upon us, and favor and honor were heaped upon us instead.

sentences.zh: 而獨于在北諸臣毛舉而概繩之，豈散秩閑曹，責反重于南樞、鳳督哉。

translations.literal: Yet for the officials in the north alone we pick out every fault and bind them all with one rope—are idle posts and minor offices to bear heavier blame than the southern command and the Fengyang post?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for officials in the north alone we pick out every fault and punish them wholesale—can minor posts bear heavier blame than the southern command and the Fengyang post?

sentences.zh: 宜摘罪狀顯著者，重懲示儆。

translations.literal: We ought to select those whose crimes are conspicuous and punish them severely as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to select those whose crimes are conspicuous and punish them severely as a warning.

sentences.zh: 若偽命未汙，身被刑辱，可置勿問。

translations.literal: If false commissions did not defile them and they suffered punishment and humiliation in person, they may be left unprosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: If they were not stained by false commissions and suffered punishment and humiliation in person, they may be left alone.

sentences.zh: 其逃避北方、俳徊而後至者，許戴罪討賊，赴臣軍前酌用。

translations.literal: Those who fled the north, lingered, and arrived later may be allowed to redeem their guilt by punishing bandits and be employed at discretion before my army.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled the north, lingered, and arrived later may redeem their guilt by fighting rebels and be employed at my discretion.

sentences.zh: 」廷議並從之。

translations.literal: " The court debate adopted all these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 傑居揚州，桀驁甚。

translations.literal: Jie dwelt at Yangzhou and was extremely arrogant and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Jie remained at Yangzhou, arrogant and ungovernable.

sentences.zh: 可法開誠佈公，導以君臣大義。

translations.literal: Kefa opened his heart with candor and guided him with the great principles of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa treated him with open candor and instructed him in the obligations of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 傑大感悟，奉約束。

translations.literal: Jie was greatly moved to understanding and submitted to discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was deeply moved and submitted to discipline.

sentences.zh: 十月，傑帥師北征。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Jie led his army on a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jie led his army north.

sentences.zh: 可法赴清江浦，遣官屯田開封，為經略中原計。

translations.literal: Kefa went to Qingjiangpu, dispatched officials to open garrison farms at Kaifeng, and planned to manage the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa went to Qingjiangpu, sent officials to open garrison farms at Kaifeng, and laid plans to recover the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮分汛地，自王家營而北至宿遷，最沖要，可法自任之，築壘緣河南岸。

translations.literal: The regional commands divided garrison zones; from Wangjiaying north to Suqian was the most critical point, which Kefa took upon himself, building ramparts along the south bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commands divided garrison zones. From Wangjiaying north to Suqian was the most critical sector, which Kefa took upon himself, building fortifications along the south bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 十一月四日，舟次鶴鎮，諜報我大清兵入宿遷。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the eleventh month, his boat anchored at He Town; spies reported that our Great Qing army had entered Suqian.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the eleventh month his boat anchored at He Town; scouts reported that Qing forces had entered Suqian.

sentences.zh: 可法進至白洋河，令總兵官劉肇基往援。

translations.literal: Kefa advanced to the White Yang River and ordered regional commander Liu Zhaoqi to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa advanced to the White Yang River and ordered regional commander Liu Zhaoqi to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 大清兵還攻邳州，肇基復援之，相持半月而解。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army then attacked Pizhou; Zhaoqi again went to its aid, and after a standoff of half a month the crisis ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army then attacked Pizhou; Zhaoqi went to its aid again, and after half a month of stalemate the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 時自成既走陝西，猶未滅，可法請頒討賊詔書，言：

translations.literal: At that time Zicheng had already fled to Shaanxi but was not yet destroyed; Kefa requested the promulgation of an edict to punish bandits, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng had fled to Shaanxi but was not yet destroyed; Kefa asked that an edict to punish the rebels be issued, writing:

sentences.zh: 自三月以來，大仇在目，一矢未加。

translations.literal: Since the third month the great enemy has been before our eyes, yet not a single arrow has been loosed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the third month our great enemy has stood before our eyes, yet not a single arrow has been loosed.

sentences.zh: 昔晉之東也，其君臣日圖中原，而僅保江左；

translations.literal: When Jin moved east, its ruler and ministers daily plotted for the Central Plain yet barely preserved the lands south of the Yangtze;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court moved east, its ruler and ministers daily plotted to recover the north yet barely held the lands south of the Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 宋之南也，其君臣盡力楚、蜀，而僅保臨安。

translations.literal: when Song moved south, its ruler and ministers exhausted their strength in Chu and Shu yet barely preserved Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: when the Song court moved south, its ruler and ministers exhausted themselves in Chu and Shu yet barely held Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 蓋偏安者，恢復之退步，未有志在偏安，而遽能自立者也。

translations.literal: For to settle for partial security is a step back from restoration; never yet has anyone whose heart was set on partial security been able at once to stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Partial security is a retreat from restoration; never yet has a court that aimed only at partial security been able to stand firm.

sentences.zh: 大變之初，黔黎灑泣，紳士悲哀，猶有朝氣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the great calamity the common people wept freely and the gentry grieved; there was still morning vigor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the great calamity common people wept and gentry grieved; there was still vigor in the land.

sentences.zh: 今則兵驕餉絀，文恬武嬉，頓成暮氣矣。

translations.literal: Now the troops are arrogant, pay is short, the civil are complacent and the martial sportive, and evening lassitude has suddenly set in.
translations.idiomatic: Now the troops are arrogant, pay is short, civil officials are complacent and military men sportive, and the land has sunk into evening lassitude.

sentences.zh: 河上之防，百未經理，人心不肅，威令不行。

translations.literal: The defenses along the river are not one percent in order; hearts are not disciplined and authority does not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The river defenses are scarcely in order; discipline has collapsed and authority no longer prevails.

sentences.zh: 復仇之師不聞及關、陝，討賊之詔不聞達燕、齊。

translations.literal: No word is heard of armies of revenge reaching Guan and Shaanxi; no word is heard of edicts to punish bandits reaching Yan and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: We hear nothing of armies of revenge reaching Guan and Shaanxi, nothing of edicts to punish rebels reaching Yan and Qi.

sentences.zh: 君父之仇，置諸膜外。

translations.literal: The debt owed father and ruler is set beyond the membrane of the eye.
translations.idiomatic: The debt owed our sovereign and father is set aside as if it did not exist.

sentences.zh: 夫我即卑宮菲食，嘗膽臥薪，聚才智精神，枕戈待旦，合方州物力，破釜沉舟，尚虞無救。

translations.literal: Even if we dwelt in low palaces and ate plain food, tasted gall and slept on brushwood, gathered all wisdom and spirit, slept on our spears awaiting dawn, combined the material strength of every province, and smashed our pots and sank our boats, we would still fear no deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we lived in humble quarters and ate plain food, tasted gall and slept on brushwood, gathered every resource of wisdom and spirit, slept on our spears awaiting dawn, and staked everything on one desperate throw, we might still fear no deliverance.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀廟堂謀畫，百執事經營，殊未盡然。

translations.literal: As I observe the court's planning and the hundred officials' management, it is far from being so.
translations.idiomatic: As I observe the court's planning and the hundred officials' management, it is far from being so.

sentences.zh: 夫將所以能克敵者，氣也；

translations.literal: What enables a general to overcome the enemy is morale;
translations.idiomatic: What enables a general to overcome the enemy is morale;

sentences.zh: 君所以能禦將者，志也。

translations.literal: what enables a ruler to control his generals is resolve.
translations.idiomatic: what enables a ruler to command his generals is resolve.

sentences.zh: 廟堂志不奮，則行間氣不鼓。

translations.literal: If the court's resolve is not ardent, then morale in the ranks will not be roused.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's resolve is not ardent, morale in the ranks cannot be roused.

sentences.zh: 夏少康不忘出竇之辱，漢光武不忘爇薪之時。

translations.literal: Xia Shaokang did not forget the shame of fleeing the cave dwelling; Han Guangwu did not forget the time when he burned brushwood.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shaokang did not forget the shame of fleeing into hiding; Han Guangwu did not forget the days when he burned brushwood for warmth.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下為少康、光武，不願左右在位，僅以晉元、宋高之說進也。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty be a Shaokang or a Guangwu, and not that those at your side advance only the counsel of Jin Yuandi and Song Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will be a Shaokang or a Guangwu, and not that those at your side advance only the counsel of Jin Yuandi and Song Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝死于賊，恭皇帝亦死于賊，此千古未有之痛也。

translations.literal: The late emperor died at the hands of bandits, and the Respectful Emperor also died at the hands of bandits—this is a pain without precedent in a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor died at rebel hands, and the Respectful Emperor likewise died at rebel hands—grief without precedent in a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 在北諸臣，死節者無多；

translations.literal: Among the officials in the north, few died maintaining their integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Among officials in the north, few died maintaining their integrity;

sentences.zh: 在南諸臣，討賊者復少。

translations.literal: among the officials in the south, few again are punishing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: among officials in the south, few are even fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 此千古未有之恥也。

translations.literal: This is a shame without precedent in a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: This is shame without precedent in a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 庶民之家，父兄被殺，尚思穴胸斷豆，得而甘心，況在朝廷，顧可漠置。

translations.literal: In a common household, when father and elder brother are killed, one still thinks of piercing the chest and severing the shins before one can be satisfied; how much more in the court—how can we set it aside indifferently?
translations.idiomatic: In an ordinary household, when father and elder brother are killed, a man still dreams of piercing the enemy's chest and severing his limbs before he can rest; how much more at court—how can we treat the matter with indifference?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下速發討賊之詔，責臣與諸鎮悉簡精銳，直指秦關，懸上爵以待有功，假便宜而責成效，絲綸之布，痛切淋漓，庶海內忠臣義士，聞而感憤也。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty swiftly issue an edict to punish bandits, charge me and the regional commands to select crack troops, strike straight for the Qin Pass, hang high ranks to await the meritorious, grant discretionary authority and demand results, and let the imperial message be issued with piercing, overflowing grief, so that loyal ministers and righteous men throughout the realm may hear and be moved to indignation.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will swiftly issue an edict to punish the rebels, charge me and the regional commands to select crack troops and strike straight for the Qin Pass, hang high rank before the meritorious, grant discretionary authority and demand results, and let the imperial message ring with piercing grief, so that loyal men throughout the realm may hear it and be stirred to action.

sentences.zh: 國家遘此大變，陛下嗣登大寶，與先朝不同。

translations.literal: The state has met this great calamity; Your Majesty has succeeded to the great throne, unlike the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: The state has met this great calamity; Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne under conditions unlike the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 諸臣但有罪之當誅，曾無功之足錄。

translations.literal: The officials have only guilt deserving execution and no merit worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Among the officials there is guilt deserving death but no merit worth recording.

sentences.zh: 今恩外加恩未已，武臣腰玉，名器濫觴。

translations.literal: Now favor is piled upon favor without end; military men wear jade at the waist and offices are lavished at the source.
translations.idiomatic: Now favor is piled upon favor without end; military men wear jade at the waist and offices are handed out indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 自後宜慎重，務以爵祿待有功，庶猛將武夫有所激厲。

translations.literal: Hereafter we ought to be cautious and reserve rank and salary for the meritorious, so that fierce generals and warriors may have something to stir them.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter we ought to be cautious and reserve rank and salary for the meritorious alone, so that fierce generals and warriors may be stirred to effort.

sentences.zh: 兵行最苦無糧，搜括既不可行，勸輸亦難為繼。

translations.literal: On campaign nothing is harder than lack of grain; exactions can no longer be carried out, and voluntary contributions are hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign nothing is harder than lack of supplies; exactions can no longer be carried out, and voluntary contributions cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 請將不急之工程，可已之繁費，朝夕之燕衎，左右之進獻，一切報罷。

translations.literal: I ask that non-urgent works, expendable costs that may be ended, daily feasting, and presents from attendants all be reported cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that non-urgent works, expendable costs, daily feasting, and presents from attendants all be cancelled at once.

sentences.zh: 即事關典禮，亦宜概從節省。

translations.literal: Even where ritual is involved, we ought generally to practice economy.
translations.idiomatic: Even where ritual is involved, we ought generally to practice economy.

sentences.zh: 蓋賊一日未滅，即有深宮曲房，錦衣玉食，豈能安享！

translations.literal: For while bandits are not destroyed in a single day, how can one dwell in deep palaces and secluded chambers and enjoy brocade robes and jade fare in peace!
translations.idiomatic: For while the rebels are not yet destroyed, how can one dwell in deep palaces and enjoy brocade robes and jade fare in peace!

sentences.zh: 必刻刻在復仇雪恥，振舉朝之精神，萃萬方之物力，盡並於送將練兵一事，庶人心可鼓，天意可回。

translations.literal: We must at every moment think of revenge and wiping away shame, rouse the court's spirit, gather the material strength of all regions, and devote it all to sending generals and training troops; then perhaps hearts may be roused and Heaven's intent turned back.
translations.idiomatic: We must at every moment think of revenge and wiping away shame, rouse the court's spirit, gather the resources of every region, and devote them all to sending generals and training troops; then perhaps hearts may be roused and Heaven's intent may turn back.

sentences.zh: 可法每繕疏，迴圈諷誦，聲淚俱下，聞者無不感泣。

translations.literal: Whenever Kefa revised a memorial he would read it round and round, voice and tears falling together, and none who heard failed to be moved to weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kefa revised a memorial he would read it again and again, voice breaking and tears falling, and none who heard him failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 比大清兵已下邳、宿，可法飛章報。

translations.literal: By then the Great Qing army had already taken Pizhou and Suqian; Kefa sent urgent memorials reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qing army had already taken Pizhou and Suqian; Kefa sent urgent memorials reporting it.

sentences.zh: 士英謂人曰：「渠欲敘防河將士功耳。

translations.literal: Shiying said to others, "He only wants to record merit for the river-defense generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying said to others, "He only wants to record merit for the river-defense generals and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」慢弗省。

translations.literal: " He was negligent and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was negligent and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 而諸鎮逡巡無進師意，且數相攻。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the regional commands hesitated with no intention of advancing, and repeatedly attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the regional commands hesitated with no intention of advancing, and repeatedly attacked one another.

sentences.zh: 明年，是為大清順治之二年，正月，餉缺，諸軍皆饑。

translations.literal: The next year was the second year of the Great Qing Shunzhi reign; in the first month pay was short and all armies were hungry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year was the second year of the Qing Shunzhi reign; in the first month pay ran short and all the armies went hungry.

sentences.zh: 頃之，河上告警。

translations.literal: Before long alarm came from along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Before long alarm came from along the river.

sentences.zh: 詔良佐、得功率師扼潁、壽，傑進兵歸、徐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liangzuo and Degong to lead armies and hold Ying and Shou, while Jie advanced toward Gui and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Liangzuo and Degong to lead armies and hold Ying and Shou, while Jie advanced toward Gui and Xu.

sentences.zh: 傑至睢州，為許定國所殺。

translations.literal: Jie reached Suizhou and was killed by Xu Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Jie reached Suizhou and was killed by Xu Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 部下兵大亂，屠睢旁近二百里殆盡。

translations.literal: His troops fell into great disorder and slaughtered nearly all within two hundred li around Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His troops fell into great disorder and slaughtered nearly everything within two hundred li of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 變聞，可法流涕頓足歎曰：「中原不可為矣。

translations.literal: When word of the upheaval came, Kefa wept, stamped his feet, and sighed, "The Central Plain can no longer be saved.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the disaster reached him, Kefa wept, stamped his feet, and cried, "The Central Plain is lost.

sentences.zh: 」遂如徐州，以總兵李本身為提督，統傑兵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to Xuzhou, made regional commander Li Benshen director-general, and took command of Jie's army.
translations.idiomatic: " He went at once to Xuzhou, made regional commander Li Benshen director-general, and took command of Jie's army.

sentences.zh: 本身者，傑甥也。

translations.literal: Benshen was Jie's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Benshen was his sister's son.

sentences.zh: 以胡茂順為督師中軍，李成棟為徐州總兵，諸將各分地，又立傑子元爵為世子，請恤於朝。

translations.literal: He made Hu Maoshun director-general's central army commander, Li Chengdong regional commander of Xuzhou, assigned each general his territory, established Jie's son Yuanjue as heir, and requested court mourning favors.
translations.idiomatic: He made Hu Maoshun central army commander of the director-general, Li Chengdong regional commander of Xuzhou, assigned each general his territory, established Jie's son Yuanjue as heir, and requested mourning favors from the court.

sentences.zh: 軍乃定。

translations.literal: The army was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was the army brought under control.

sentences.zh: 傑軍既還，於是大樑以南皆不守。

translations.literal: Once Jie's army had returned, south of Daliang nothing was defended.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jie's army had withdrawn, everything south of Kaifeng was left undefended.

sentences.zh: 土英忌可法威名，加故中允衛胤文兵部右侍郎，總督興平軍，以奪可法權。

translations.literal: Shiying resented Kefa's prestige and promoted the former bachelor of arts Wei Yinwen to right vice minister of war and director-general of the Xingping army to strip Kefa of power.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying resented Kefa's prestige and promoted the former bachelor of arts Wei Yinwen to right vice minister of war and director-general of the Xingping army to strip Kefa of authority.

sentences.zh: 胤文，傑同鄉也，陷賊南還，傑請為己監軍。

translations.literal: Yinwen was Jie's fellow townsman; he had fallen to the bandits and returned south, and Jie requested him as his own supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yinwen was Jie's fellow townsman; he had surrendered to the rebels and returned south, and Jie had requested him as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 傑死，胤文承士英旨，疏誚可法。

translations.literal: When Jie died, Yinwen followed Shiying's intent and memorialized to reproach Kefa.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie died, Yinwen followed Shiying's intent and memorialized to reproach Kefa.

sentences.zh: 士英喜，故有是命，駐揚州。

translations.literal: Shiying was pleased, and for this reason the appointment was made; he was stationed at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was pleased, and for this reason the appointment was made; Yinwen was stationed at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，可法還揚州。

translations.literal: In the second month Kefa returned to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Kefa returned to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，得功來襲興平軍，城中大懼。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Degong came to attack the Xingping army and the city was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Degong attacked the Xingping army and panic seized the city.

sentences.zh: 可法遣官講解。

translations.literal: Kefa dispatched an official to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa sent an official to mediate.

sentences.zh: 乃引去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Degong then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時大兵已取山東、河南北，逼淮南。

translations.literal: At that time the great army had already taken Shandong and north Henan and pressed upon Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: By then the main army had taken Shandong and northern Henan and was pressing upon Huainan.

sentences.zh: 四月朔，可法移軍駐泗州，護祖陵。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month Kefa moved his army to station at Sizhou to guard the imperial ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month Kefa moved his army to Sizhou to guard the imperial ancestral tombs.

sentences.zh: 將行，左良玉稱兵犯闕，召可法入援。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Zuo Liangyu raised troops and attacked the capital; Kefa was summoned to enter and aid.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Zuo Liangyu raised troops against the court and Kefa was summoned to the capital's aid.

sentences.zh: 渡江抵燕子磯，得功已敗良玉軍。

translations.literal: He crossed the river and reached Swallow Rock Jetty; Degong had already defeated Liangyu's army.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river to Swallow Rock Jetty, where he learned that Degong had already defeated Liangyu's army.

sentences.zh: 可法乃趨天長，檄諸將救盱眙。

translations.literal: Kefa then hastened to Tianchang and issued orders to the generals to rescue Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa then hastened to Tianchang and ordered the generals to rescue Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 俄報盱眙已降大清，泗州援將侯方岩全軍沒。

translations.literal: Before long word came that Xuyi had already surrendered to the Great Qing, and the Sizhou relief commander Hou Fangyan's entire army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long word came that Xuyi had surrendered to the Qing, and Hou Fangyan, the relief commander at Sizhou, had lost his entire army.

sentences.zh: 可法一日夜奔還揚州。

translations.literal: Kefa raced back to Yangzhou in a day and a night.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa raced back to Yangzhou in a day and a night.

sentences.zh: 訛傳定國兵將至，殲高氏部曲。

translations.literal: A false report spread that Dingguo's troops were about to arrive and annihilate Gao's followers.
translations.idiomatic: A false report spread that Dingguo's troops were about to arrive and annihilate Gao's followers.

sentences.zh: 城中人悉斬關出，舟楫一空。

translations.literal: Everyone in the city broke through the gates and fled; boats were emptied entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the city broke through the gates and fled; every boat was gone.

sentences.zh: 可法檄各鎮兵，無一至者。

translations.literal: Kefa issued summons to the troops of each regional command, yet not one came.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa called up the armies of every regional command, but not a single unit answered.

sentences.zh: 二十日，大清兵大至，屯班竹園。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day, Great Qing troops arrived in force and encamped at Banzhu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth the Qing army arrived in full strength and made camp at Banzhu Garden.

sentences.zh: 明日，總兵李棲鳳、監軍副使高岐鳳拔營出降，城中勢益單。

translations.literal: The next day Regional Commander Li Qifeng and Supervisory Deputy Commissioner Gao Qifeng broke camp and surrendered; the city's strength grew ever more isolated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Qifeng, regional commander, and Gao Qifeng, supervisory deputy commissioner, broke camp and surrendered, leaving the city's defenses ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 諸文武分陴拒守。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials each took sections of the wall to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials divided the walls among themselves and held their posts.

sentences.zh: 舊城西門險要，可法自守之。

translations.literal: The western gate of the old city was strategically critical; Kefa personally guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: The western gate of the old city was the vital point; Kefa took charge of its defense himself.

sentences.zh: 作書寄母妻，且曰：「死葬我高皇帝陵側。

translations.literal: He wrote a letter to send to his mother and wife, saying moreover: "When I die, bury me beside the tomb of the Gaozu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to his mother and wife, adding: "When I die, bury me beside the Gaozu Emperor's tomb.

sentences.zh: 」越二日，大清兵薄城下，砲擊城西北隅，城遂破。

translations.literal: " Two days later Great Qing troops pressed against the foot of the city; cannon struck the northwest corner of the wall, and the city was then breached.
translations.idiomatic: " Two days later the Qing army reached the walls; cannon fire shattered the northwest corner, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 可法自刎不殊，一參將擁可法出小東門，遂被執。

translations.literal: Kefa attempted suicide by cutting his own throat but was not fatally wounded; a staff colonel supported Kefa and brought him out the Small East Gate, whereupon he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa cut his throat but failed to kill himself; a staff colonel led him out through the Small East Gate, where he was captured.

sentences.zh: 可法大呼曰：「我史督師也。

translations.literal: Kefa shouted loudly, saying: "I am Supervising Secretary Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa cried out: "I am Supervising Secretary Shi!

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " With that they killed him.

sentences.zh: 揚州知府任民育，同知曲從直、王纘爵，江都知縣周志畏、羅伏龍，兩淮鹽運使楊振熙，監餉知縣吳道正，江都縣丞王志端，賞功副將汪思誠，幕客盧渭等皆死。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Prefect Ren Minyu; Vice Prefects Qu Congzhi and Wang Zuojue; Jiangdu Magistrates Zhou Zhiwei and Luo Fulong; Lianghuai Salt Transport Commissioner Yang Zhenxi; Provisions Supervising Magistrate Wu Daozheng; Jiangdu Assistant Magistrate Wang Zhiduan; Reward-granting Vice General Wang Sicheng; and staff member Lu Wei all died.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Minyu, prefect of Yangzhou; Qu Congzhi and Wang Zuojue, vice prefects; Zhou Zhiwei and Luo Fulong, magistrates of Jiangdu; Yang Zhenxi, Lianghuai salt transport commissioner; Wu Daozheng, provisions supervising magistrate; Wang Zhiduan, Jiangdu assistant magistrate; Wang Sicheng, reward-granting vice general; and the staff member Lu Wei—all perished.

sentences.zh: 可法初以定策功加少保兼太子太保，以太后至加少傅兼太子太傅，敘江北戰功加少師兼太子太師，擒劇盜程繼孔功加太傅，皆力辭，不允。

translations.literal: Initially, for his merit in settling the enthronement policy, Kefa was promoted to Junior Guardian concurrent with Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; when the empress dowager arrived he was promoted to Junior Mentor concurrent with Mentor to the Heir Apparent; for recounting northern Jiang campaign merits he was promoted to Junior Preceptor concurrent with Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; for capturing the notorious bandit Cheng Jikong he was promoted to Grand Preceptor—all these he vigorously declined, and his refusal was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: For helping fix the enthronement he was offered Junior Guardian and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; when the empress dowager arrived, Junior Mentor and Mentor to the Heir Apparent; for victories in northern Jiang, Junior Preceptor and Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; for capturing the notorious bandit Cheng Jikong, Grand Preceptor—each time he refused forcefully, and each time the court refused to let him.

sentences.zh: 後以宮殿成，加太師，力辭，乃允。

translations.literal: Later, when the palace halls were completed, he was promoted to Grand Preceptor; he vigorously declined, and only then was his refusal granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace was finished he was again offered Grand Preceptor; he declined forcefully, and this time the court accepted his refusal.

sentences.zh: 可法為督師，行不張蓋，食不重味，夏不箑，冬不裘，寢不解衣。

translations.literal: As supervising secretary Kefa traveled without an umbrella canopy, ate no second dish at a meal, used no fan in summer, wore no fur in winter, and slept without undressing.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary he went without a parasol over his chair, ate a single dish at each meal, used no fan in summer and no fur in winter, and never unrobed to sleep.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，無子，其妻欲置妾。

translations.literal: Past forty years of age and without a son, his wife wished to take a concubine for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was past forty and had no son; his wife wanted to bring in a concubine.

sentences.zh: 太息曰：「王事方殷，敢為兒女計乎！

translations.literal: He sighed deeply and said: "State affairs are at their height—how dare I reckon as to sons and daughters!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "State business presses upon us—how can I be scheming for a household?

sentences.zh: 」歲除遣文牒，至夜半，倦索酒。

translations.literal: " On New Year's Eve he was dispatching documents; by midnight he was weary and asked for wine.
translations.idiomatic: " On New Year's Eve he was still sending out documents; by midnight, exhausted, he called for wine.

sentences.zh: 庖人報殽肉已分給將士，無可佐者，乃取鹽鼓下之。

translations.literal: The cook reported that meat dishes had already been divided and given to officers and troops and there was nothing to accompany the wine, so he took salt and drank it down.
translations.idiomatic: The cook said the meat had already been portioned out to the troops and there was nothing to go with the wine, so he took salt and drank it down with that.

sentences.zh: 可法素善飲，數鬥不亂，在軍中絕飲。

translations.literal: Kefa had always been skilled at drinking and could drink several piculs without becoming disorderly, but in the army he abstained entirely from wine.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa had always been a strong drinker who could hold several piculs without staggering, yet in camp he kept entirely sober.

sentences.zh: 是夕，進數十觥，思先帝，泫然淚下，憑幾臥。

translations.literal: That evening he drank dozens of cups; thinking of the late emperor he shed tears copiously, then leaned against the desk and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: That night he drank dozens of cups; as he thought of the late emperor tears streamed down his face, and he lay his head on the desk.

sentences.zh: 比明，將士集轅門外，門不啟，左右遙語其故。

translations.literal: When dawn came, officers and troops gathered outside the camp gate; the gate was not opened, and attendants called out at a distance to explain why.
translations.idiomatic: By morning officers and soldiers had assembled outside headquarters, but the gate stayed shut while attendants called out the reason from a distance.

sentences.zh: 知府民育曰：「相公此夕臥，不易得也。

translations.literal: Prefect Ren Minyu said: "The Chancellor's lying down this night is not easily come by.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Ren Minyu said: "The Chancellor actually sleeping tonight is a rare thing.

sentences.zh: 」命鼓人仍擊四鼓，戒左右毋驚相公。

translations.literal: " He ordered the drummer to continue striking the fourth watch drum and warned those at hand not to startle the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the watch-drums to hold at the fourth watch and told the attendants not to wake the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 須臾，可法寤，聞鼓聲，大怒曰：「誰犯吾令！

translations.literal: In a moment Kefa awoke, heard the drum, and said in great anger: "Who violated my order!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kefa woke, heard the drums, and raged: "Who defied my command!

sentences.zh: 」將士述民育意，乃獲免。

translations.literal: " Officers and soldiers explained Minyu's intent, and they were then spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " When the officers explained Minyu's reason, he spared them.

sentences.zh: 嘗孑處鈴閣或舟中，有言宜警備者，曰：「命在天。

translations.literal: Once when he was alone in the command pavilion or on a boat, someone said he should be on alert and take precautions; he said: "Fate lies with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once, alone in headquarters or aboard his boat, when someone urged him to keep a tighter guard he said: "Life and death are Heaven's to decide.

sentences.zh: 」可法死，覓其遺骸。

translations.literal: " After Kefa died they searched for his remains.
translations.idiomatic: " After Kefa's death they searched for his body.

sentences.zh: 天暑，眾屍蒸變，不可辯識。

translations.literal: The weather was hot; the corpses of the multitude putrefied and changed, and could not be distinguished and identified.
translations.idiomatic: In the heat the piled corpses decayed beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 逾年，家人舉袍笏招魂，葬于揚州郭外之梅花領。

translations.literal: After more than a year, his family raised his robe and court tablet to summon the soul and buried him at Meihua Ridge outside the walls of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later his family performed a soul-summoning rite with his robe and court tablet and buried him at Meihua Ridge outside Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後四方弄兵者，多假其名號以行，故時謂可法不死雲。

translations.literal: Afterward, those who raised arms throughout the four directions often borrowed his name and title to act, and so at the time it was said that Kefa had not died.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward rebels across the land often used his name to lend legitimacy to their cause, so people said Kefa was still alive.

sentences.zh: 可法無子，遺命以副將史德威為之後。

translations.literal: Kefa had no son; by final testament he made Vice General Shi Dewei his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa had no son and left orders naming Vice General Shi Dewei as his heir.

sentences.zh: 有弟可程，崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: He had a younger brother Ke Cheng, a jinshi of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother, Ke Cheng, who passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 擢庶起士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a bachelor for the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a bachelor selected for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，降賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, he surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing fell he submitted to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，南歸，可法請置之理。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated he returned south; Kefa requested that he be placed under the law.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated he fled south, and Kefa asked that he be tried for his crime.

sentences.zh: 王以可法故，令養母。

translations.literal: The prince for Kefa's sake ordered him to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: For Kefa's sake the prince regent spared him and ordered him only to support their mother.

sentences.zh: 可程遂居南京，後流寓宜興，閱四十年而卒。

translations.literal: Ke Cheng then lived in Nanjing; later he wandered and settled in Yixing, and after forty years died.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Cheng lived in Nanjing, later drifted to Yixing, and died there forty years on.

sentences.zh: 任民育，字時澤，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Ren Minyu, styled Shize, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Minyu, courtesy name Shize, came from Jining.

sentences.zh: 天啟中鄉舉，善騎射。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi era he passed the provincial exams and was adept at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 真定巡撫徐標請於朝，用為贊畫，理屯事。

translations.literal: Zhending Grand Coordinator Xu Biao memorialized the court and had him employed as staff planner, managing garrison-farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Biao, grand coordinator of Zhending, petitioned the court to appoint him staff planner in charge of garrison-farming.

sentences.zh: 真定失，南還。

translations.literal: When Zhending was lost, he returned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhending fell he fled south.

sentences.zh: 福王時，授亳州知州。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu's reign he was appointed prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 以才擢揚州知府，可法倚之。

translations.literal: For his talent he was promoted to prefect of Yangzhou, and Kefa relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing his ability, the court promoted him to prefect of Yangzhou, where Kefa came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 城破，緋衣端坐堂上，遂見殺，闔家男婦盡赴井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he sat upright in crimson robes in the hall and was killed; the whole household, men and women, all threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he sat upright in his crimson official robes in the hall and was slain; every man and woman in his household threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 從直，遼東人，與其子死東門。

translations.literal: Congzhi was from Liaodong; he and his son died at the East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi, a native of Liaodong, died at the East Gate together with his son.

sentences.zh: 纘爵，鄞人，工部尚書佐孫。

translations.literal: Zuojue was from Yin county, grandson of a Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zuojue, from Yin county, was a grandson of a former Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 志畏，亦鄞人，進士，年少好氣，數遭傑將士窘辱，求解職。

translations.literal: Zhiwei was also from Yin, a jinshi; young and hot-tempered, he repeatedly suffered humiliation from outstanding generals and officers and asked to leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei, also from Yin and a jinshi, was young and quick-tempered; after repeated humiliation by senior generals and officers he asked to be relieved of his post.

sentences.zh: 會伏龍至，可法命代之。

translations.literal: When Fulong arrived, Kefa ordered him to replace Zhiwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Fulong arrived, Kefa ordered him to take Zhiwei's place.

sentences.zh: 伏龍，新喻人。

translations.literal: Fulong was from Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: Fulong was a native of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 故梓潼知縣，受代甫三日。

translations.literal: Formerly district magistrate of Zitong; he had taken over the post only three days before.
translations.idiomatic: He had formerly been magistrate of Zitong and had held his new post only three days.

sentences.zh: 振熙，臨海人。

translations.literal: Zhenxi was from Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxi came from Linhai.

sentences.zh: 道正，余姚人。

translations.literal: Daozheng was from Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Daozheng was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 志端，孝豐人。

translations.literal: Zhiduan was from Xiaofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiduan came from Xiaofeng.

sentences.zh: 思誠，字純一，貴池人。

translations.literal: Sicheng, styled Chunyi, was from Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng, courtesy name Chunyi, was from Guichi.

sentences.zh: 渭，字渭生，長洲諸生，可法出鎮淮、揚，謂等伏闕上書，言：「秦檜在內，李綱居外，宋終北轅。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Weisheng, a licentiate of Changzhou—when Kefa went out to command Huai and Yang, Wei and others lay prostrate at the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying: "Qin Hui was inside and Li Gang was outside, and Song finally turned its chariot northward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, courtesy name Weisheng, a licentiate of Changzhou—when Kefa went out to command Huai and Yang, Wei and others prostrated themselves at the palace gate and submitted a memorial: "With Qin Hui inside the court and Li Gang kept outside, Song ended by turning its chariot north."

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 居禮賢館久，可法才渭。

translations.literal: He had lived long at the Hall for Honoring the Worthy; Kefa valued Wei's talent.
