translations.idiomatic: After lodging long at the Hall for Honoring the Worthy, Kefa came to prize Wei's ability.

sentences.zh: 渭方歲貢，當得官，不受職，而擬授昆山歸昭等二十余人為通判、推官、知縣。

translations.literal: Wei had just been nominated by annual tribute and was due to receive office, but he would not take a post; instead he proposed appointing more than twenty men including Gui Zhao of Kunshan as sub-prefects, investigating censors, and district magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had just been nominated through the annual tribute route and was eligible for office, but he refused a post for himself and instead proposed appointing more than twenty men, including Gui Zhao of Kunshan, as sub-prefects, investigating censors, and district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 甫二旬，城陷，渭監守鈔關，投於河。

translations.literal: Only twenty days later the city fell; Wei was supervising the tax barrier at Caoguan and threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Barely twenty days later the city fell; Wei, who was supervising the Caoguan tax barrier, drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 昭死西門，從死者十七人。

translations.literal: Zhao died at the West Gate; seventeen followed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao died at the West Gate, and seventeen others died with him.

sentences.zh: 時同守城死者，又有遵義知府何剛、庶起士吳爾壎。

translations.literal: Those who also died defending the city at that time included Zunyi Prefect He Gang and bachelor-selected-for-Hanlin Wu Erxun.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died defending the city included He Gang, prefect of Zunyi, and Wu Erxun, a bachelor selected for the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 而揚州諸生殉養者，有高孝纘、王士琇、王纘、王績、王續等。

translations.literal: Among the licentiates of Yangzhou who died in martyrdom were Gao Xiaozuan, Wang Shixiu, Wang Zuan, Wang Ji, Wang Xu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Yangzhou licentiates who died for the cause were Gao Xiaozuan, Wang Shixiu, Wang Zuan, Wang Ji, Wang Xu, and others.

sentences.zh: 又有武生戴之籓、醫者陳天拔、畫士陸愉、義兵張有德、市民馮應昌、舟子徐某，並自盡。

translations.literal: Also a military licentiate Dai Zhifan, physician Chen Tianba, painter Lu Yu, militiaman Zhang Youde, townsman Feng Yingchang, and a boatman surnamed Xu—all took their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: A military licentiate, Dai Zhifan; a physician, Chen Tianba; a painter, Lu Yu; a militiaman, Zhang Youde; a townsman, Feng Yingchang; and a boatman surnamed Xu—all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 他婦女死節者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Other women who died preserving their integrity cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The women who died defending their honor are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 何剛，字愨人，上海人。

translations.literal: He Gang, styled Keren, was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Gang, courtesy name Keren, came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 見海內大亂，慨然有濟世之志。

translations.literal: Seeing great disorder throughout the realm, he was filled with resolve to save the world.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos engulf the realm, he resolved to serve the common good.

sentences.zh: 交天下豪俊，與東陽許都善，語之曰：「子所居天下精兵處，盍練一旅以待用。

translations.literal: He befriended heroes and men of talent under Heaven; he was on good terms with Xu Du of Dongyang and said to him: "The place where you dwell is where the finest troops under Heaven are; why not drill a company and hold them ready for use?
translations.idiomatic: He sought out heroes across the land and was close to Xu Du of Dongyang, to whom he said: "You live where the finest soldiers in the realm are found—why not drill a company and keep them ready?

sentences.zh: 」都諾而去。

translations.literal: " Xu assented and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu agreed and departed.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，入都上書，言：「國家設制科，立資格，以約束天下豪傑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year he entered the capital and submitted a memorial, saying: "The state established the examination system and set qualifications to constrain the heroes under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year he went to the capital and submitted a memorial: "The state created the examination system and fixed qualifications to keep the realm's bold spirits in check.

sentences.zh: 此所以弭亂，非所以戡亂也。

translations.literal: This is how one quells disorder, not how one conquers disorder.
translations.idiomatic: That is a way to quiet disorder, not to crush it.

sentences.zh: 今日救生民，匡君國，莫急於治兵。

translations.literal: Today to save the people and rectify the ruler and state, nothing is more urgent than governing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Today, to save the people and restore the ruler and realm, nothing is more urgent than putting the army in order.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠簡強壯英敏之士，命知兵大臣教習之，講韜鈐，練筋骨，拓膽智，時召而試之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will truly select strong, alert, and keen men, command military ministers who understand warfare to instruct them, study strategy, train sinews and bone, expand courage and wisdom, and summon them from time to time to test them.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will truly choose strong, keen men and charge military ministers who understand war to train them—teaching strategy, hardening body and nerve, sharpening courage and wit, and testing them from time to time—

sentences.zh: 學成優其秩，寄以兵柄，必能建奇功。

translations.literal: When their training is complete, honor their ranks and entrust them with military authority—they will surely be able to achieve extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: then, once trained, honor them with rank, entrust them with command, and they will surely win extraordinary victories.

sentences.zh: 臣讀戚繼光書，繼光數言義烏、東陽兵可用。

translations.literal: Your subject has read Qi Jiguang's writings; Jiguang repeatedly said that Yiwu and Dongyang troops were usable.
translations.idiomatic: I have read Qi Jiguang's works, in which he repeatedly says that troops from Yiwu and Dongyang are worth using.

sentences.zh: 誠得召募數千，加之訓練，准繼光遺法，分佈河南郡縣，大寇可平。

translations.literal: If several thousand can truly be recruited and trained according to Jiguang's methods, distributed among the commanderies and districts of Henan, the great bandits can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit several thousand men, train them by Jiguang's methods, and station them across the commanderies and districts of Henan—the great bandits can be crushed.

sentences.zh: 」因薦都及錢塘進士姚奇胤、桐城諸生周岐、陝西諸生劉湘客、絳州舉人韓霖。

translations.literal: " He then recommended Du, Yao Qiyin jinshi of Qiantang, Zhou Qi licentiate of Tongcheng, Liu Xiangke licentiate of Shaanxi, and Han Lin provincial graduate of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recommended Xu Du, Yao Qiyin of Qiantang, jinshi, Zhou Qi, licentiate of Tongcheng, Liu Xiangke, licentiate of Shaanxi, and Han Lin, provincial graduate of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，即擢剛職方主事，募兵金華。

translations.literal: The emperor found his words bold and at once promoted Gang to secretary in the Ministry of War bureau and ordered him to raise troops at Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed by his words and at once promoted Gang to secretary in the Ministry of War and ordered him to raise troops at Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 而都作亂已前死，霖亦為賊用，剛不知，故並薦之。

translations.literal: But Du had already risen in rebellion and died before this, and Lin was also employed by the rebels—Gang did not know this, and so recommended them together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du had already rebelled and died, and Han Lin was also serving the rebels—Gang did not know this and recommended them both.

sentences.zh: 剛出都，都城陷，馳還南京。

translations.literal: Gang had left the capital when the capital city fell; he galloped back to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Gang had just left the capital when it fell; he raced back to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊逼京師，剛友陳子龍、夏允彝將聯海舟達天津，備緩急，募卒二千人，至是令剛統之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when rebels pressed the capital, Gang's friends Chen Zilong and Xia Yunyi were going to link sea boats to reach Tianjin as a reserve for emergencies; they recruited two thousand soldiers, and at this time Gang was ordered to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when rebels threatened the capital, his friends Chen Zilong and Xia Yunyi planned to link up sea vessels to reach Tianjin as a reserve force and raised two thousand men; Gang was now ordered to command them.

sentences.zh: 子龍入為兵科，言防江莫如水師，更乞廣行召募，委剛訓練，從之。

translations.literal: Zilong entered service as an officer of the military affairs section and said that for defending the river nothing matched a naval force; he again requested broad recruitment and entrusted training to Gang—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong entered the military affairs section and argued that river defense depended above all on a navy; he again asked for broad recruitment and entrusted training to Gang, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 剛乃上疏言：「臣請陛下三年之內，宮室不必修，百官禮樂不必備。

translations.literal: Gang then submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject asks that within three years Your Majesty need not repair palaces and halls, and need not fully equip the rites and music of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gang then submitted a memorial: "I ask that for three years Your Majesty need not repair palaces or halls, and need not fully restore the rites and music of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 惟日救天下才，智者決策，廉者理財，勇者禦敵。

translations.literal: Only daily rescue the talents under Heaven—the wise to decide policy, the incorrupt to manage finances, the brave to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Only rescue talent daily—the wise to decide policy, the incorrupt to manage funds, the brave to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 爵賞無出此三者，則國富兵強，大敵可服。

translations.literal: If enfeoffments and rewards go no outside these three types, then the state will be rich and the army strong, and great enemies can be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: If honors and rewards go only to these three kinds of men, the state will grow rich, the army strong, and great enemies can be overcome.

sentences.zh: 若以驕悍之將馭無制之兵，空言恢復，是卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: If arrogant, fierce generals command undisciplined troops while empty words speak of recovery, that is walking backward while seeking to go forward.
translations.idiomatic: If arrogant, unruly generals lead undisciplined troops while empty talk speaks of reconquest, that is walking backward and calling it advance.

sentences.zh: 優遊歲月，潤色偏安，錮豪傑于草間，迫梟雄為盜賊，是株守以待盡也。

translations.literal: Idling away the months, embellishing a partial peace, locking heroes in the grass and driving bold chieftains to become bandits—that is standing rooted in place awaiting exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: To idle away the months, polish a precarious peace, lock heroes in obscurity, and drive bold men into banditry—that is to stand still and wait for ruin.

sentences.zh: 惟廟堂不以浮文取士，而以實績課人，則真才皆為國用，而議論亦省矣。

translations.literal: Only if the court does not take men by florid prose but assesses people by real achievement, then true talent will all serve the state and wrangling over words will also be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: If the court stops choosing men by florid essays and judges them by real achievement, true talent will serve the state and empty debate will shrink.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者羅草澤英豪，得才多者受上賞，則梟傑皆畢命封疆，而盜魁亦少矣。

translations.literal: Send envoys in all directions to gather heroes from grass and marshes; those who obtain the most talent receive the highest reward—then bold chieftains will all exhaust their lives on the borders, and bandit chiefs will also be fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys far and wide to gather heroes from the wilds; reward most those who find the most talent—then bold men will spend their lives on the frontier, and bandit chiefs will grow fewer.

sentences.zh: 東南人滿，徙之江北，或賜爵，或贖罪，則豪右皆盡力南畝，而軍餉亦充矣。

translations.literal: The southeast is crowded with people; relocate them to north of the river, whether by granting noble rank or redeeming crimes—then the powerful gentry will all exert themselves in the southern fields, and military provisions will also be filled.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast is overcrowded; relocate people to the north, whether by granting rank or allowing crimes to be redeemed—then the gentry will work the fields and military supplies will be filled.

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time none of this could be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 尋進本司員外郎，以其兵隸史可法。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to assistant director in the same bureau, and his troops were placed under Shi Kefa's command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to assistant director in the same bureau, and his troops were placed under Shi Kefa's command.

sentences.zh: 可法大喜得剛，剛亦自喜遇可法知已。

translations.literal: Kefa was greatly delighted to obtain Gang; Gang also rejoiced at meeting in Kefa a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa was overjoyed to have Gang; Gang in turn rejoiced at finding in Kefa a true confidant.

sentences.zh: 士英惡之，出剛遵義知府。

translations.literal: Shi Ying hated him and sent Gang out as prefect of Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ying disliked him and had him posted as prefect of Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 可法垂涕曰：「子去，吾誰仗？

translations.literal: Kefa shed tears and said: "When you go, upon whom shall I rely?
translations.idiomatic: Kefa wept and said: "When you leave, whom shall I rely on?

sentences.zh: 」剛亦泣，願死生無相背。

translations.literal: " Gang also wept and vowed that in life and death they would not turn against each other.
translations.idiomatic: " Gang wept as well and vowed that in life or death they would not forsake each other.

sentences.zh: 逾月，揚州被圍，佐可法拒守。

translations.literal: More than a month later Yangzhou was besieged; he assisted Kefa in resisting and holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later Yangzhou was besieged, and he helped Kefa hold the city.

sentences.zh: 城破，投井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 吳爾壎，崇德人。

translations.literal: Wu Erxun was from Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Erxun came from Chongde.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士，授庶起士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, he was appointed bachelor selected for the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, he was appointed a bachelor selected for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 賊敗南還，謁可法，請從軍贖罪，可法遂留參軍事。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and returned south; he visited Kefa, asked to join the army to redeem his guilt, and Kefa then retained him to participate in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were routed and withdrew south, he went to see Kefa and asked to serve in the army to atone for his past; Kefa kept him on as a military adviser.

sentences.zh: 其父子屏方督學福建，爾壎斷一指畀故人祝淵曰：「君歸語我父母，悉出私財畀我餉軍。

translations.literal: His father Wu Ziping was then supervising education in Fujian; Erxun cut off a finger and gave it to his old friend Zhu Yuan, saying: "When you return, tell my parents to give out all their private wealth to supply my army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu Ziping was then serving as provincial education commissioner in Fujian. Erxun severed a finger and gave it to his old friend Zhu Yuan, saying: "When you go back, tell my parents to give me all their private funds for army supplies.

sentences.zh: 我他日不歸，以指葬可也。

translations.literal: If I do not return another day, you may bury this finger in my stead.
translations.idiomatic: If I never come home, bury this finger in my place.

sentences.zh: 」從高傑北征至睢州，傑被難，爾壎流寓祥符。

translations.literal: " He followed Gao Jie on the northern expedition to Suizhou; Jie met calamity, and Erxun drifted to Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched north with Gao Jie as far as Suizhou; when Jie was killed, Erxun took refuge in Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 遇一婦人，自言福王妃。

translations.literal: He encountered a woman who declared herself the consort of Prince Fu.
translations.idiomatic: There he met a woman who claimed to be Prince Fu's consort.

sentences.zh: 爾壎因守臣附疏以進，詔斥其妄言，逮之，可法為救免。

translations.literal: Erxun had the local official attach a memorial to present it; an edict denounced his wild talk and ordered his arrest, but Kefa interceded and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Erxun had the local magistrate forward a memorial on his behalf; the court condemned his story as false and ordered his arrest, but Kefa pleaded for him and won his release.

sentences.zh: 後守揚州新城，投井死。

translations.literal: Later he defended the new city of Yangzhou and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the new walled quarter of Yangzhou and drowned himself in a well when it fell.

sentences.zh: 高弘圖，字研文，膠州人。

translations.literal: Gao Hongtu, styled Yanwen, was a native of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hongtu, courtesy name Yanwen, came from Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Secretariat and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Secretariat secretary and then promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 柧棱自持，不依麗人。

translations.literal: Upright and principled in self-restraint, he did not rely on powerful patrons.
translations.idiomatic: Principled and self-disciplined, he refused to depend on influential protectors.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，陳時政八患，請用鄒元標、趙南星。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he set forth eight afflictions of the times and requested the employment of Zou Yuanbiao and Zhao Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he memorialized on eight ills plaguing government and urged the appointment of Zou Yuanbiao and Zhao Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 巡按陝西，題薦屬吏，趙南星糾之，弘圖不能無望，代還，移疾去。

translations.literal: As touring censor of Shaanxi he recommended subordinate officials in a memorial; Zhao Nanxing impeached him; Hongtu could not be without resentment; when replaced and returned, he pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: While touring censor in Shaanxi he promoted subordinates in a memorial, but Zhao Nanxing attacked him for it. Hongtu nursed a grievance; when his term ended he went home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢亟攻東林，其黨以弘圖嘗與南星有隙，召起弘圖故官。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian urgently attacked the Donglin faction; his clique, because Hongtu had once had a rift with Nanxing, recalled Hongtu to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei Zhongxian pressed his assault on the Donglin, his followers recalled Hongtu to his old office, counting on his past quarrel with Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 入都，則楊漣、左光鬥、魏大中等已下詔獄，鍛煉嚴酷。

translations.literal: When he entered the capital, Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and others had already been sent to the edict prison, and the torture in fabricating charges was severe.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital, Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, Wei Dazhong, and others were already in the edict prison, suffering brutal interrogation.

sentences.zh: 弘圖果疏論南星，然言「國是已明，雷霆不宜頻擊」，「詔獄諸臣，生殺宜聽司敗法」，則頗謂忠賢過當者。

translations.literal: Hongtu indeed submitted a memorial discussing Nanxing, yet said "the nation's consensus is already clear; thunderbolts ought not strike repeatedly," and "for the ministers in the edict prison, life and death should be left to the judicial officials' law" — in which he somewhat considered Zhongxian excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu did memorialize against Nanxing, but he also wrote that "the court's verdict is settled and the thunder of punishment should not fall again and again," and that "those in the edict prison should live or die according to the law" — language that plainly judged Zhongxian too harsh.

sentences.zh: 疏中又引漢元帝乘船事，忠賢方導帝遊幸，不悅，矯旨切責之。

translations.literal: In the memorial he also cited the Han Emperor Yuan's boat incident; Zhongxian was then guiding the emperor on tours of pleasure and was displeased, forging an edict to rebuke him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial also cited Emperor Yuan of Han's boating episode; Zhongxian, who was then steering the emperor toward pleasure tours, took offense and had a forged edict issued to rebuke him severely.

sentences.zh: 後諫帝毋出蹕東郊，又極論前陝西巡撫喬應甲罪，又嘗語刺崔呈秀。

translations.literal: Later he admonished the emperor not to go out with the imperial guard to the eastern suburbs; he also exhaustively argued the crimes of the former Shaanxi grand coordinator Qiao Yingjia; he also once spoke in barbed language against Cui Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: He later warned the emperor against leaving the eastern suburbs under full guard, denounced the former Shaanxi governor Qiao Yingjia at length, and once made pointed remarks against Cui Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 呈秀、應甲皆忠賢黨，由是忠賢大怒，擬順天巡按不用。

translations.literal: Chengxiu and Yingjia were both Zhongxian's party; thereby Zhongxian was greatly angered and proposed not to employ him as touring censor of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu and Yingjia were Wei Zhongxian's men, and Zhongxian, furious, blocked his appointment as Shuntian touring censor.

sentences.zh: 弘圖乞歸，遂令閑住。

translations.literal: Hongtu requested to return home; he was then ordered to idle at home.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu asked to retire and was sent home to live in enforced idleness.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，起故官。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen's accession brought him back to his old office.

sentences.zh: 劾罪田詔、劉志選、梁夢環。

translations.literal: He impeached and convicted Tian Zhao, Liu Zhixuan, and Liang Menghuan.
translations.idiomatic: He secured convictions against Tian Zhao, Liu Zhixuan, and Liang Menghuan.

sentences.zh: 擢太僕少卿，復移疾去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then again pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of the Imperial Stud, he once more cited illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 三年春，召拜左僉都御史，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was summoned and appointed Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief, then advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was called to serve as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and soon promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 五年遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he moved to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 方入署，總理戶、工二部中官張彝憲來會，弘圖恥之，不與共坐，七疏乞休。

translations.literal: Just as he entered the yamen, the eunuch Zhang Yixian, who superintended both the Households and Works departments, came to meet; Hongtu was shamed by this, would not sit together with him, and seven times submitted memorials requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: On his first day in office the eunuch Zhang Yixian, who oversaw both Revenue and Works, came to call; Hongtu found the visit degrading, refused to share a seat, and seven times asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遂削籍歸，家居十年不起。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; his name was struck from the rolls and he returned home, living at home ten years without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath stripped him from the register; he went home and did not serve again for ten years.

sentences.zh: 十六年，召拜南京兵部右侍郎，就遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, then immediately transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was recalled as Nanjing vice minister of war and at once made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，京師陷，福王立，改弘圖禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month the capital fell; Prince Fu was established; Hongtu was changed to Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell the following third month and Prince Fu took the throne, Hongtu became minister of rites and grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 疏陳新政八事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth eight items of the new administration.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on eight points of the new regime.

sentences.zh: 一，宣義問。

translations.literal: First, proclaim righteous inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: First: proclaim the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 請聲逆賊之罪，鼓發忠義。

translations.literal: He requested to proclaim the crimes of the rebel bandits and rouse loyal righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that the rebels' crimes be denounced publicly to stir loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 一，勤聖學。

translations.literal: Second, diligently pursue sacred learning.
translations.idiomatic: Second: cultivate the emperor's learning.

sentences.zh: 請不俟釋服，日禦講筵。

translations.literal: He requested not to wait until mourning garb was laid aside, but daily to preside over the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that lectures resume at once, without waiting for mourning dress to end.

sentences.zh: 一，設記注。

translations.literal: Third, establish recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Third: appoint diarists.

sentences.zh: 請召詞臣入侍，日記言動。

translations.literal: He requested to summon literary officials to attend and daily record words and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that literary officials attend court each day to keep a record of the emperor's words and acts.

sentences.zh: 一，睦親籓。

translations.literal: Fourth, harmonize with the imperial clans.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: reconcile with the princely houses.

sentences.zh: 請如先朝踐極故事，遣官齎璽書慰問。

translations.literal: He requested, as in former dynasties' accession precedents, to dispatch officials bearing seal letters to console and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Following earlier enthronement custom, he asked that envoys be sent with sealed letters of reassurance to the imperial clans.

sentences.zh: 一，議廟祀。

translations.literal: Fifth, deliberate on temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: settle ritual worship.

sentences.zh: 請權附列聖神主於奉先殿，仍於孝陵側望祀列聖山陵。

translations.literal: He requested provisionally to attach the spirit tablets of successive emperors in the Hall of Ancestors, and still at Xiaoling's side to perform distant sacrifices toward the tombs of successive emperors.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed temporarily placing the spirit tablets of past emperors in the Hall of Ancestors while offering distant rites toward their tombs from beside the Xiaoling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 一，嚴章奏。

translations.literal: Sixth, strictly regulate memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: tighten control of memorials.

sentences.zh: 請禁奸宄小人藉端妄言，脫罪僥倖。

translations.literal: He requested to prohibit wicked petty men from taking pretexts for wild speech to escape guilt by luck.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to stop scheming petty men from using reckless accusations as a pretext to evade punishment.

sentences.zh: 一，收人心。

translations.literal: Seventh, win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: recover popular support.

sentences.zh: 請蠲江北、河南、山東田租，毋使賊徒藉口。

translations.literal: He requested to remit land rent in Jiangbei, Henan, and Shandong, lest bandits take pretext.
translations.idiomatic: He urged remission of land tax in Jiangbei, Henan, and Shandong so rebels could not use hardship as an excuse.

sentences.zh: 一，擇詔使。

translations.literal: Eighth, select edict envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: choose imperial envoys.

sentences.zh: 請遣官招諭朝鮮，示牽制之勢。

translations.literal: He requested to dispatch officials to summon and instruct Korea, showing a posture of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed sending envoys to Korea with edicts of reassurance, displaying a strategy of tying down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 並褒納焉。

translations.literal: All were praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised and adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝廷大議多出弘圖手。

translations.literal: At that time the court's major deliberations mostly came from Hongtu's hand.
translations.idiomatic: In those days most weighty court decisions bore Hongtu's imprint.

sentences.zh: 馬士英疏薦阮大鋮，弘圖不可。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying submitted a memorial recommending Ruan Dacheng; Hongtu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying memorialized to recommend Ruan Dacheng, but Hongtu refused.

sentences.zh: 士英曰：「我自任之。

translations.literal: Shiying said: "I will take responsibility myself.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying said: "I will answer for it myself.

sentences.zh: 」乃命大鋮假冠帶陛見。

translations.literal: " Then Dacheng was ordered to don provisional cap and sash and attend audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: " Dacheng was then allowed cap and sash and summoned to an audience.

sentences.zh: 大鋮入見，曆陳冤狀，以弘圖不附東林引為證。

translations.literal: Dacheng entered audience and sequentially detailed his grievances, citing as proof that Hongtu had not adhered to the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Dacheng laid out his grievances at length, pointing to Hongtu's distance from the Donglin as evidence in his favor.

sentences.zh: 弘圖則力言逆案不可翻，大鋮、士英並怒。

translations.literal: Hongtu staunchly declared the treason case could not be overturned; Dacheng and Shiying were both angry.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu insisted the treason verdict must stand; Dacheng and Shiying were enraged.

sentences.zh: 一日，閣中語及故庶起士張溥，士英曰：「我故人也，死，酹而哭之。

translations.literal: One day in the cabinet they spoke of the former Hanlin bachelor Zhang Pu; Shiying said: "He was an old friend of mine; when he died I poured libation and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the privy council they mentioned the late Hanlin bachelor Zhang Pu; Shiying said: "He was my friend; when he died I offered wine and mourned him.

sentences.zh: 」薑曰廣笑曰：「公哭東林者，亦東林耶？

translations.literal: " Jiang Yueguang laughed and said: "Sir, you weep for Donglin men — are you also Donglin?
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Yueguang smiled and said: "You weep for Donglin men — does that make you one of them?

sentences.zh: 」士英曰：「我非畔東林者，東林拒我耳。

translations.literal: " Shiying said: "I am not one who betrayed Donglin; Donglin rejected me, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiying replied: "I did not turn against the Donglin; they shut me out.

sentences.zh: 」弘圖因縱臾之，士英意解。

translations.literal: " Hongtu then encouraged him in this, and Shiying's mind was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongtu chimed in to soothe him, and Shiying's resentment eased.

sentences.zh: 而劉宗周劾疏自外至，大鋮宣言曰廣實使之，於是士英怒不可止。

translations.literal: But Liu Zongzhou's impeaching memorial arrived from outside; Dacheng proclaimed that Yueguang had actually instigated it; thus Shiying's anger could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Zongzhou's impeachment arrived from outside; Dacheng claimed Yueguang had put him up to it, and Shiying's fury knew no check.

sentences.zh: 而薦張捷、謝升之疏出，朝端益水火矣。

translations.literal: Then memorials recommending Zhang Jie and Xie Sheng appeared; at court the situation grew ever more like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials pushing Zhang Jie and Xie Sheng followed, and court factions drew further apart like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 內劄用戶部侍郎張有譽為尚書，弘圖封還，具奏力諫，卒以廷推簡用。

translations.literal: An internal note appointed Vice Minister Zhang Youyu of Revenue as Minister; Hongtu sealed and returned it, fully memorializing and strongly remonstrating; in the end selection by court recommendation was used.
translations.idiomatic: An inner draft made Revenue vice minister Zhang Youyu minister; Hongtu returned it sealed with a forceful protest, and the post was filled by regular court recommendation.

sentences.zh: 中官議設東廠，弘圖爭不得。

translations.literal: Eunuchs proposed establishing the Eastern Depot; Hongtu argued but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs moved to restore the Eastern Depot, Hongtu fought the plan and lost.

sentences.zh: 遂乞休，不許，加太子少師，改戶部尚書，文淵閣。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement; not permitted; he was given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, changed to Minister of Revenue, Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire but was refused; instead he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent, minister of revenue, and grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 尋以太后至，進太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, because the empress dowager arrived, he was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager reached the capital he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，弘圖四疏乞休，乃許之。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Hongtu four times submitted memorials requesting retirement; then he was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Hongtu four times asked to leave office and was finally allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 弘圖既謝政，無家可歸，流寓會稽。

translations.literal: Hongtu having left office, with no home to return to, drifted and resided in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office and homeless, Hongtu wandered and settled in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 國破，逃野寺中，絕粒而卒。

translations.literal: When the state was destroyed he fled to a wilderness temple and died by ceasing grain.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty collapsed he hid in a country temple and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 姜曰廣，字居之，新建人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yueguang, styled Juzhi, was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yueguang, courtesy name Juzhi, came from Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末，舉進士，授庶起士，進編修。

translations.literal: Near the end of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination; he was appointed a Hanlin bachelor and advanced to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wanli reign he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and rose to compiler.

sentences.zh: 天啟六年奉使朝鮮，不攜中國一物往，不取朝鮮一錢歸，朝鮮人為立懷潔之碑。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianqi he was sent on mission to Korea; he carried not one object from China going and took not one coin from Korea returning; the Koreans erected for him a stele of cherishing purity.
translations.idiomatic: On a Tianqi sixth-year mission to Korea he took nothing from China and brought nothing back; the Koreans raised a stele honoring his integrity.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，魏忠賢黨以曰廣東林，削其藉。

translations.literal: The next summer Wei Zhongxian's faction, because Yueguang was Donglin, stripped his registration.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer Wei's faction struck him from the rolls as a Donglin man.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起右中充。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was recalled as Right Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen came to the throne he was restored as right reader in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 九年，積官至吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, by accumulated promotion, he reached Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year he had risen to right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐事左遷南京太常卿，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: After a demotion to Nanjing director of imperial sacrifices he pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 十五年，起詹事，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled as Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, directing the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he returned as tutor to the heir apparent and head of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嘗言：「曰廣在講筵，言詞激切，朕知其人。

translations.literal: Chongzhen once said: "Yueguang at the lecture hall — his words sharp and impassioned — I know the man.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen once remarked: "When Yueguang speaks at lectures his language is fierce; I know what sort of man he is.

sentences.zh: 」每優容之。

translations.literal: " He always treated him with special forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 北都變聞，諸大臣議所立。

translations.literal: When word of the northern capital's upheaval arrived, the great ministers deliberated whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: News of the fall of the northern capital set the ministers debating who should reign.

sentences.zh: 曰廣、呂大器用周鑣、雷縯祚言，主立潞王，而諸帥奉福籓至江上。

translations.literal: Yueguang and Lü Daqi adopted the words of Zhou Biao and Lei Yanzuo, advocating establishing the Prince of Lu; but the various commanders escorted the Fu fief to the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang and Lü Daqi, following Zhou Biao and Lei Yanzuo, favored enthroning the Prince of Lu, while the generals were already bringing Prince Fu's house to the river.

sentences.zh: 於是文武官並集內官宅，韓贊周令各署名籍。

translations.literal: Thereupon civil and military officials all gathered at the eunuch's residence; Han Zanzhou ordered each to sign a register.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials then assembled at an eunuch's house, where Han Zanzhou had them sign a roll.

sentences.zh: 曰廣曰：「無遽，請祭告奉先殿而後行。

translations.literal: Yueguang said: "Do not rush; please perform sacrificial announcement at the Hall of Ancestors before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang said: "We must not hurry; let us offer sacrifice at the Hall of Ancestors first.

sentences.zh: 」明日至奉先殿，諸勳臣語侵史可法，曰廣呵之，於是群小鹹目攝曰廣。

translations.literal: " The next day at the Hall of Ancestors the meritorious lords' words encroached on Shi Kefa; Yueguang rebuked them; thus the petty men all glared threateningly at Yueguang.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day at the Hall of Ancestors the nobles' remarks turned against Kefa; Yueguang scolded them, and the lesser men fixed hostile stares on him.

sentences.zh: 廷推閣臣，以曰廣異議不用，用史可法、高弘圖、馬士英。

translations.literal: In court recommendation for grand secretaries, because of Yueguang's dissent he was not used; Shi Kefa, Gao Hongtu, and Ma Shiying were used.
translations.idiomatic: When grand secretaries were chosen by court vote, Yueguang was passed over for his dissent; Shi Kefa, Gao Hongtu, and Ma Shiying were appointed.

sentences.zh: 及再推詞臣，以王鐸、陳子壯、黃道周名上，而首曰廣。

translations.literal: When literary officials were recommended again, the names Wang Duo, Chen Zizhuang, and Huang Daozhou went up, with Yueguang first.
translations.idiomatic: A second recommendation for literary grand secretaries listed Wang Duo, Chen Zizhuang, and Huang Daozhou, with Yueguang at the top.

sentences.zh: 乃改曰廣禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與鐸並命。

translations.literal: Then Yueguang was changed to Minister of Rites and concurrently Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, appointed together with Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang was then made minister of rites and Eastern Pavilion grand secretary, appointed alongside Duo.

sentences.zh: 鐸未至，可法督師揚州，曰廣與弘圖協心輔政。

translations.literal: Duo had not arrived; Kefa supervised armies at Yangzhou; Yueguang and Hongtu cooperated in assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: Before Duo reached the capital, Kefa was commanding at Yangzhou, and Yueguang worked in concert with Hongtu to run the government.

sentences.zh: 而士英挾擁戴功，內結勳臣硃國弼、劉孔昭、趙之龍，外連諸鎮劉澤清、劉良佐等，謀擅朝權，深忌曰廣。

translations.literal: But Shiying wielded the merit of supporting the establishment; inwardly he allied with the meritorious lords Zhu Guobi, Liu Kongzhao, and Zhao Zhilong; outwardly he connected with the garrison commanders Liu Zeqing, Liu Liangzuo, and others; he schemed to monopolize court power and deeply envied Yueguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying, however, traded on his role in enthroning Prince Fu, bonded inside with nobles Zhu Guobi, Liu Kongzhao, and Zhao Zhilong and outside with regional commanders Liu Zeqing and Liu Liangzuo, and plotted to dominate the court while resenting Yueguang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，士英特薦起阮大鋮。

translations.literal: Before long Shiying specially recommended recalling Ruan Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shiying pushed a special recall of Ruan Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 曰廣力爭不得，遂乞休，言：

translations.literal: Yueguang strongly argued but could not prevail; then he requested retirement, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang fought the appointment in vain and resigned, writing:

sentences.zh: 前見文武交競，既慚無術調和；

translations.literal: Earlier I saw civil and military officials contending and was ashamed that I had no art to harmonize them;
translations.idiomatic: I have lately watched civil and military men clash and been ashamed that I could not reconcile them;

sentences.zh: 近睹逆案忽翻，又愧不能寢弭。

translations.literal: Recently I saw the treason case suddenly overturned and again was ashamed that I could not suppress and quiet it.
translations.idiomatic: I have now seen the treason verdict reversed and been ashamed that I could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 遂棄先帝十七年之定力，反陛下數日前之明詔。

translations.literal: Thus the late emperor's seventeen years of steadfast resolve were abandoned, and Your Majesty's clear edict of a few days ago was reversed.
translations.idiomatic: This abandons the late emperor's seventeen-year resolve and overturns the clear edict Your Majesty issued only days ago.

sentences.zh: 臣請以前事言之。

translations.literal: Your subject requests to speak by prior events.
translations.idiomatic: Let me speak from what has already happened.

sentences.zh: 臣觀先帝之善政雖多，而以堅持逆案為尤美；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that though the late emperor's good policies were many, holding firm to the treason case was especially admirable;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor did much that was good, but above all he held fast to the treason verdict;

sentences.zh: 先帝之害政間有，而以頻出口宣為亂階。

translations.literal: though the late emperor's harmful policies were occasional, frequent oral edicts were the ladder to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: his misgovernment was sporadic, yet repeated verbal orders opened the way to chaos.

sentences.zh: 用閣臣內傳矣，用部臣勳臣內傳矣，用大將用言官內傳矣。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries were appointed by inner transmission; ministry officials and meritorious lords by inner transmission; great generals and remonstrating officials by inner transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries came by palace relay, ministry officials and nobles by palace relay, generals and censors by palace relay.

sentences.zh: 而所得閣臣，則淫貪巧猾之周延儒也，逢君朘民奸險刻毒之溫體仁、楊嗣昌也，偷生從賊之魏藻德也；

translations.literal: Yet the grand secretaries obtained were the lecherous, greedy, and cunning Zhou Yanru; the flatterers of the ruler and exploiters of the people, the treacherous and cruel Wen Tiren and Yang Sichang; and Wei Zaode, who clung to life and followed the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries chosen were the dissolute and scheming Zhou Yanru, the sycophantic and ruthless Wen Tiren and Yang Sichang, and Wei Zaode, who saved himself by joining the rebels;

sentences.zh: 所得部臣，則陰邪貪狡之王永光、陳新甲；

translations.literal: the ministry officials obtained were the secretly wicked and greedy Wang Yongguang and Chen Xinji;
translations.idiomatic: the ministers picked were the covertly corrupt Wang Yongguang and Chen Xinji;

sentences.zh: 所得勳臣，則力阻南遷盡撤守禦狂稚之李國禎；

translations.literal: the meritorious lords obtained were Li Guozhen, who forcefully blocked southern relocation and wholly withdrew defenses, reckless and immature;
translations.idiomatic: the nobles chosen included Li Guozhen, who blocked flight south and stripped the capital of defenders in reckless folly;

sentences.zh: 所得大將，則紈絝支離之王樸、。

translations.literal: the great generals obtained were the dissolute and incompetent Wang Pu,
translations.idiomatic: the generals chosen were the pampered and useless Wang Pu,

sentences.zh: 倪寵；

translations.literal: Ni Chong;
translations.idiomatic: and Ni Chong;

sentences.zh: 所得言官，則貪橫無賴之史褷、陳啟新也。

translations.literal: the remonstrating officials obtained were Shi Shen and Chen Qixin, greedy, overbearing, and unscrupulous;
translations.idiomatic: the censors chosen were the grasping and brazen Shi Shen and Chen Qixin;

sentences.zh: 凡此皆力排眾議，簡目中旨，後效可睹。

translations.literal: all these forcefully excluded collective opinion, selected per the imperial intent, and the subsequent results can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: In every case dissent was overridden, favorites were picked to match the throne's wish, and the consequences speak for themselves.

sentences.zh: 今又不然。

translations.literal: Now again it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Now the pattern has returned.

sentences.zh: 不必僉同，但求面對，立談取官。

translations.literal: There is no need for unanimous agreement; one need only seek a face-to-face audience and obtain office by talk on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Unanimity is dispensed with; a private audience and a few flattering words suffice for appointment.

sentences.zh: 陰奪會推之柄，陽避中旨之名，決廉恥之大防，長便佞之惡習。

translations.literal: Covertly they seize the power of collective recommendation, overtly they avoid the name of imperial selection, break the great barrier of integrity and shame, and foster the evil habit of flattery.
translations.idiomatic: They quietly strip the court of its power to nominate, publicly deny that the choice comes from the throne, tear down the wall of honor, and nourish sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 此豈可訓哉！

translations.literal: How can this serve as a model!
translations.idiomatic: What precedent is this!

sentences.zh: 臣待罪綸扉，苟好盡言，終蹈不測之禍。

translations.literal: Your subject holds office at the privy council in guilt; if he delights in speaking fully, he will ultimately meet unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I serve at the privy council on sufferance; speak my mind and I court ruin.

sentences.zh: 聊取充位，又來鮮恥之譏。

translations.literal: If he merely occupies the seat, he again invites the reproach of shamelessness.
translations.idiomatic: Stay silent and I invite the charge of holding office without honor.

sentences.zh: 願乞骸骨還鄉里。

translations.literal: I wish to beg my bones and return to my home district.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to retire to my home.

sentences.zh: 得旨慰留，士英、大鋮等滋不悅。

translations.literal: He received an edict reassuring and retaining him; Shiying, Dacheng, and others grew more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with words of comfort and kept him on; Shiying, Dacheng, and their allies were only the more aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 國弼、孔昭遂以誹謗先帝，誣衊忠臣李國禎為言，交章攻之。

translations.literal: Guobi and Kongzhao then attacked him in successive memorials, citing slander of the late emperor and calumniating the loyal minister Li Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Guobi and Kongzhao thereupon filed memorial after memorial accusing him of insulting the late emperor and defaming the loyal Li Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 劉澤清故附東林，擁立議起，亦主潞王。

translations.literal: Liu Zeqing had formerly attached to the Donglin faction; when the enthronement dispute arose he also favored Prince Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeqing had once sided with the Donglin party and, when the succession was debated, had also backed Prince Lu.

sentences.zh: 至是入朝，則力詆東林以自解免。

translations.literal: At this time entering court, he forcefully denounced Donglin to exculpate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he came to court, he vilified the Donglin faction to clear his own name.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「中興所恃在政府。

translations.literal: He also said: "Restoration depends on the government.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "National revival rests on the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 今用輔臣，宜令大帥僉議。

translations.literal: In appointing assisting ministers now, the great commanders should jointly deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When choosing grand secretaries, the field marshals ought to have a collective say.

sentences.zh: 」曰廣愕然。

translations.literal: " Yueguang was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: " Yueguang stared in disbelief.

sentences.zh: 越數日，澤清疏劾呂大器、雷縯祚，而薦張捷、鄒之麟、張孫振、劉光鬥等。

translations.literal: Several days later Zeqing memorialized impeaching Lu Daqi and Lei Yunzuo, while recommending Zhang Jie, Zou Zhilin, Zhang Sunzhen, Liu Guangdou, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Zeqing impeached Lu Daqi and Lei Yunzuo and recommended Zhang Jie, Zou Zhilin, Zhang Sunzhen, Liu Guangdou, and others.

sentences.zh: 已，又請免故輔周延儒髒。

translations.literal: Afterward he again requested exemption of burial honors for the former grand secretary Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that burial honors be denied the late grand secretary Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 曰廣曰：「是欲漸幹朝政也。

translations.literal: Yueguang said: "This is seeking gradually to meddle in court government.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang said: "This is a step toward meddling in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 」乃下部議，竟不許。

translations.literal: " It was sent down for ministry deliberation and ultimately not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal went to the ministries for review and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 曰廣嘗與士英交詆王前。

translations.literal: Yueguang had once exchanged reviling words with Shiying before the king.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang and Shiying had already traded insults in the prince's presence.

sentences.zh: 宗室硃統钅類者，素無行，士英啖以官，使擊曰廣。

translations.literal: Among the imperial clan was Zhu Tong, who had always been without conduct; Shiying fed him with office and had him attack Yueguang.
translations.idiomatic: There was an imperial clansman named Zhu Tong, a man of bad character whom Shiying bought with office and set against Yueguang.

sentences.zh: 澤清又假諸鎮疏攻劉宗周及曰廣，以三案舊事及迎立異議為言，請執下法司，正謀危君父之罪。

translations.literal: Zeqing also forged memorials from various garrisons attacking Liu Zongzhou and Yueguang, citing the three-case old affairs and differing opinions on enthronement, requesting arrest and handover to the judiciary to establish the crime of plotting against sovereign and father.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing also fabricated petitions in the name of the regional armies against Liu Zongzhou and Yueguang, invoking the old factional cases and the dispute over enthronement, and demanded they be handed to the courts on charges of treason against sovereign and father.

sentences.zh: 頃之，統钅類復劾曰廣五大罪，請並劉士楨、王重、楊廷麟、劉宗周、陳必謙、周鑣、雷縯祚置之理，必謙、鑣以是逮。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Tong again impeached Yueguang on five major crimes, requesting that Liu Shizhen, Wang Chong, Yang Tinglin, Liu Zongzhou, Chen Biqian, Zhou Biao, and Lei Yunzuo all be brought to trial; Biqian and Biao were arrested on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tong impeached Yueguang again on five capital charges and asked that Liu Shizhen, Wang Chong, Yang Tinglin, Liu Zongzhou, Chen Biqian, Zhou Biao, and Lei Yunzuo be tried together; Biqian and Biao were arrested accordingly.

sentences.zh: 曰廣既連遭誣衊，屢疏乞休，其年九月始得請。

translations.literal: Yueguang having repeatedly suffered slander, memorialized many times requesting retirement; only in the ninth month of that year was he granted leave.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of calumnies Yueguang petitioned repeatedly to resign; permission came only in the ninth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 入辭，諸大臣在列。

translations.literal: Entering to bid farewell, the various grand ministers were in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to take leave, the senior ministers were all present.

sentences.zh: 曰廣曰：「微臣觸忤權奸，自分萬死，上恩寬大，猶許歸田。

translations.literal: Yueguang said: "This humble subject offended powerful villains and resigned himself to ten thousand deaths; the sovereign's grace is broad and still permits return to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang said: "Your servant offended men in power and expected death; the throne has been merciful and still allows me to go home.

sentences.zh: 臣歸後，願陛下以國事為重。

translations.literal: After your subject returns, I pray Your Majesty will prioritize state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, I beg Your Majesty to put the realm first.

sentences.zh: 」士英熟視曰廣，詈曰：「我權奸，汝且老而賊也。

translations.literal: " Shiying stared fixedly at Yueguang and cursed: "I am a powerful villain — and you are an old traitor besides.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiying fixed his eyes on Yueguang and snarled: "So I am the villain in power — and you, old man, are a traitor to boot.

sentences.zh: 」既出，復於朝堂相詬詈而罷。

translations.literal: " After exiting, they again reviled each other in the court hall and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Once outside, they continued shouting abuse at each other in the hall before parting.

sentences.zh: 曰廣骨鯁，扼於憸邪，不竟其用，遂歸。

translations.literal: Yueguang was upright and uncompromising, stifled by wicked ministerial villains, did not fulfill his use, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang was a man of stiff integrity, checked by corrupt ministers at court, and left office before he could accomplish what he had set out to do.

sentences.zh: 其後左良玉部將金聲桓者，已降於我大清，既而反江西，迎曰廣以資號召。

translations.literal: Afterward Zuo Liangyu's subordinate general Jin Shenghuan, who had already surrendered to our Great Qing, then rebelled in Jiangxi and welcomed Yueguang to lend prestige to his call.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin Shenghuan, a lieutenant of Zuo Liangyu who had surrendered to the Qing and then rebelled in Jiangxi, brought Yueguang in to lend his name to the cause.

sentences.zh: 聲桓敗，曰廣投偰家池死。

translations.literal: When Shenghuan was defeated, Yueguang threw himself into the Xie family pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenghuan fell, Yueguang drowned himself in the Xie family pool.

sentences.zh: 初，鑣世父尚書應秋、叔父御史維持，以附魏忠賢並麗逆案，鑣恥之。

translations.literal: Initially, Biao's uncle by senior generation Minister Yingqiu and uncle by junior generation Censor Weichi were implicated in the Li treason case for attaching to Wei Zhongxian; Biao was ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Biao's grand-uncle the minister Yingqiu and his uncle the censor Weichi had been caught up in the Li treason case through their ties to Wei Zhongxian, and Biao was ashamed of the stain.

sentences.zh: 通籍後，即交東林，矯矯樹名節。

translations.literal: After entering the register, he immediately associated with Donglin and resolutely cultivated reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered official life he joined the Donglin circle and made a conspicuous show of moral rectitude.

sentences.zh: 及被放，與宣城沈壽民讀書茅山，廷臣多論薦之。

translations.literal: When dismissed, he studied on Maoshan with Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng; court officials often discussed and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he studied on Mount Mao with Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng, and many at court spoke up on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 十五年起禮部主事，進郎中，為吏部尚書鄭三俊所倚。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was raised to Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites, promoted to Director, and relied upon by Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became a clerk in the Ministry of Rites, rose to director, and won the trust of the minister of personnel Zheng Sanjun.

sentences.zh: 然為人好名，頗飾偽，給事中韓如愈疏論之，罷歸。

translations.literal: Yet as a man he loved fame and somewhat adorned himself with pretense; Supervising Secretary Han Ruyu memorialized criticizing him and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: But he craved reputation and was widely thought to play the part; Supervising Secretary Han Ruyu denounced him in a memorial, and he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 福王立于南京。

translations.literal: Prince Fu was established at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu was enthroned at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 馬士英既逐呂大器，以鑣及雷縯祚曾立潞王議，令硃統钅類劾曰廣，因言鑣、縯祚等皆曰廣私黨，請悉置於理，遂令逮治。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying having already driven out Lu Daqi, because Biao and Lei Yunzuo had favored Prince Lu for enthronement, had Zhu Tong impeach Yueguang, and thereby said Biao, Yunzuo, and others were all Yueguang's private faction, requesting all be brought to trial; they were ordered arrested and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Shiying had ousted Lu Daqi, he used Biao's and Yunzuo's earlier support for Prince Lu as a pretext, had Zhu Tong impeach Yueguang, and declared Biao, Yunzuo, and the rest Yueguang's private clique; all were ordered arrested.

sentences.zh: 而士英劾鑣從弟鐘從逆，並及鑣。

translations.literal: Shiying also impeached Biao's younger cousin by the same grandfather Zhong for following rebellion, extending the charge to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying further charged Biao's cousin Zhong with rebellion and implicated Biao as well.

sentences.zh: 鐘亦逮治。

translations.literal: Zhong was also arrested and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was arrested too.

sentences.zh: 阮大鋮居金陵時，諸生顧杲等出《留都防亂公揭》討之，主之者鑣也，大鋮以故恨鑣。

translations.literal: When Ruan Dacheng resided at Jinling, the students Gu Gao and others issued the "Public Manifesto of Nanking to Guard against Disorder" attacking him; Biao was the organizer; Dacheng therefore resented Biao.
translations.idiomatic: While Ruan Dacheng was living in Nanjing, the student Gu Gao and others published the Public Manifesto against Disorder in the Southern Capital denouncing him; Biao had led the effort, and Dacheng never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 鑣獄急，屬御史陳丹衷求解于士英，為緝事者所獲，丹衷出為長沙知州。

translations.literal: Biao's imprisonment was urgent; he entrusted Censor Chen Danzhong to seek release from Shiying; this was discovered by investigators; Danzhong was sent out as prefect of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: As Biao's case grew desperate he asked Censor Chen Danzhong to intercede with Shiying; investigators caught wind of it, and Danzhong was banished to be prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 於是察處御史羅萬爵希大鋮指，上疏痛詆鑣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Investigating Censor Luo Wanjue, hoping to match Dacheng's intent, submitted a memorial fiercely denouncing Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Luo Wanjue, eager to please Dacheng, then filed a savage denunciation of Biao.

sentences.zh: 而光祿卿祁逢吉，鑣同邑人，見人輒詈鑣，遂得為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: And Director of Imperial Sacrifices Qi Fengji, a fellow townsman of Biao, wherever he met people would revile Biao; he thus obtained appointment as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fengji of the Directorate of Sacrifices, a townsman of Biao's, won promotion to vice minister of revenue by reviling Biao at every turn.

sentences.zh: 亡何，左良玉稱兵檄討士英罪，言引用大鋮，構陷鑣、縯祚，鍛煉周內。

translations.literal: Before long Zuo Liangyu raised troops and issued a proclamation denouncing Shiying's crimes, saying he had brought in Dacheng, framed Biao and Yunzuo, and tortured and imprisoned them inside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zuo Liangyu took up arms and issued a manifesto against Shiying, accusing him of installing Dacheng, framing Biao and Yunzuo, and torturing them within the palace compound.

sentences.zh: 士英、大鋮益怒。

translations.literal: Shiying and Dacheng grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying and Dacheng were only the more enraged.

sentences.zh: 大鋮謂鑣實召良玉兵，王乃賜鑣、縯祚自盡，鐘棄市。

translations.literal: Dacheng claimed Biao had actually summoned Liangyu's troops; the king then granted Biao and Yunzuo death by suicide, and Zhong was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng insisted that Biao had summoned Liangyu's army; the prince then ordered Biao and Yunzuo to take their own lives and had Zhong executed in public.

sentences.zh: 雷縯祚，太湖人。

translations.literal: Lei Yunzuo was a native of Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yunzuo came from Taihu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exams in the third year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 十三年夏，帝思破格用人，而考選止及進士，特命舉人貢生就試教職者，悉用為部寺司屬推官知縣，凡二百六十三人，號為庚辰特用。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirteenth year the emperor wished to appoint men outside regular channels, but the examination and selection reached only jinshi; he specially ordered juren, tribute students, and those who had tested for teaching posts to all be used as bureau clerks in ministries and directorates, investigating censors, and county magistrates — 263 in all — called the special gengchen appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the thirteenth year the emperor wanted to break with convention in appointments, yet the regular selection process reached only jinshi degree holders; he therefore ordered all juren, tribute students, and teaching candidates to be placed in ministry and directorate posts, as censors and county magistrates — 263 men in all — known as the special gengchen appointments.

sentences.zh: 而縯祚得刑部主事。

translations.literal: Yunzuo obtained the post of Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzuo was made a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 明年三月劾楊嗣昌六大罪可斬，鳳陽總督硃大典、安慶巡撫鄭二陽、河南巡撫高名衡、山東巡撫王公弼宜急易，帝不悅。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year he impeached Yang Sichang on six major crimes warranting execution, and said Zhu Dadian, governor-general of Fengyang; Zheng Eryang, grand coordinator of Anqing; Gao Mingheng, grand coordinator of Henan; and Wang Gongbi, grand coordinator of Shandong, should be urgently replaced; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he charged Yang Sichang with six capital offenses and demanded the immediate replacement of Zhu Dadian at Fengyang, Zheng Eryang at Anqing, Gao Mingheng at Henan, and Wang Gongbi at Shandong; the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 十五年擢武德道兵備僉事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Military Preparation Vice Commissioner of Wude Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to military intendant of Wude Circuit.

sentences.zh: 山東被兵，縯祚守德州，有詔獎勵。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered military attack; Yunzuo defended Dezhou; an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong came under attack Yunzuo held Dezhou, and the throne issued words of praise.

sentences.zh: 乃疏劾督師範志完縱兵淫掠，折除軍餉，構結大黨。

translations.literal: He then memorialized impeaching Superintendent Fan Zhwan for letting troops plunder licentiously, deducting military pay, and forming a great faction.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached the superintendent Fan Zhwan for allowing his troops to loot at will, skimming military pay, and building a faction.

sentences.zh: 帝心善其言，以淫掠事責兵部，而令糸寅祚再陳。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly approved his words, blamed the Ministry of War on the plundering matter, and ordered Yunzuo to state more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was inclined to believe him, rebuked the Ministry of War over the looting, and told Yunzuo to elaborate.

sentences.zh: 志完者，首輔周延儒門生也，縯祚意有所忌，久不奏。

translations.literal: Zhwan was chief assistant Zhou Yanru's disciple; Yunzuo had some apprehension in mind and long did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Zhwan was a protégé of the chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru, and Yunzuo, mindful of the risk, held back his memorial for a long time.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，延儒下廷議，寅祚乃奏言：「志完兩載僉事，驟陟督師，非有大黨，何以至是。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year Yanru was sent down for court deliberation; Yunzuo then memorialized saying: "Zhwan after two years as vice commissioner was suddenly promoted superintendent; without a great faction how could this have come about?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year Yanru was referred to court for deliberation; Yunzuo then submitted: "Zhwan rose from vice commissioner to superintendent in only two years — without a powerful faction behind him, how could that happen?

sentences.zh: 大僚則尚書范景文等，詞林則諭德方拱乾等，言路則給事中硃徽、沈胤培、袁彭年等，皆其黨也。

translations.literal: Among great officials there are Minister Fan Jingwen and others; among the Hanlin, Reader Fang Gongqian and others; among the remonstrance channels, Supervising Secretaries Zhu Hui, Shen Yinpei, Yuan Pengnian, and others — all are his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers such as Fan Jingwen, Hanlin readers such as Fang Gongqian, and supervising secretaries such as Zhu Hui, Shen Yinpei, and Yuan Pengnian — all belong to his clique.

sentences.zh: 方德州被攻，不克去，掠臨清，又五日，志完始至。

translations.literal: Just as Dezhou was under attack he could not leave; he plundered Linqing; only after five more days did Zhwan arrive.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezhou was besieged he would not budge, sent his men to plunder Linqing, and only showed up five days later.

sentences.zh: 聞後部破景州，則大懼，欲避入德州城。

translations.literal: Hearing that the rear force had taken Jingzhou, he was greatly afraid and wished to avoid into Dezhou city.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the enemy rear guard had taken Jingzhou he panicked and wanted to hide inside Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 漏三下，邀臣議。

translations.literal: At the third watch of night he invited your subject to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch he summoned me to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 臣不聽，志完乃偕流寓詞臣拱乾見臣南城古廟。

translations.literal: Your subject refused to listen; Zhwan then came with the sojourning literary official Gongqian to see your subject at an ancient temple in the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: I refused; Zhwan then brought the displaced literary official Gongqian to find me at an old temple in the southern quarter.

sentences.zh: 臣告以督師非入城官，薊州失事，由降丁內潰，志完不懌而去。

translations.literal: Your subject told him the superintendent was not an official who enters cities; the Jizhou failure was due to surrendered troops collapsing internally; Zhwan left displeased.
translations.idiomatic: I told him a superintendent has no business entering a walled city, and that the loss at Jizhou came of defectors within the ranks; Zhwan stalked off in a fury.

sentences.zh: 若夫座主當朝，罔利曲庇，只手有燎原之勢，片語操生死之權，稱功頌德，遍于班聯。

translations.literal: As for his patron in power, disregarding profit and bending to protect him — with one hand he had the force of a prairie fire, with one phrase he held the power of life and death; praising merit and extolling virtue pervaded the whole assembly.
translations.idiomatic: His patron at court shields him for gain; with one hand he can kindle a prairie fire, with one word he can decide who lives or dies, and the whole court sings his praises.

sentences.zh: 臣不忍見陛下以周、召待大臣，而大臣以嚴嵩、傅國觀自待也。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear to see Your Majesty treat great ministers as the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao while great ministers treat themselves as Yan Song and Fu Guanyun.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to watch Your Majesty honor your ministers as the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao honored theirs, while they conduct themselves like Yan Song and Fu Guanyun.

sentences.zh: 臣外籓小吏，乙榜孤蹤，不言不敢，盡言不敢，感陛下虛懷俯納，故不避首輔延儒與舉國媚附時局，略進一言。

translations.literal: Your subject is a minor official from an outer province, a solitary track of the second rank — not to speak he dares not, to speak fully he dares not; moved by Your Majesty's open mind bowing to receive, he therefore does not avoid the chief assistant Yanru and the whole nation's flattering attachment to the times, and briefly advances one word.
translations.idiomatic: I am a minor provincial official of the second rank, alone and without backing — afraid to speak, yet more afraid to stay silent; moved by Your Majesty's willingness to listen, I venture one word against Chief Grand Secretary Yanru and the nation's habit of flattering power.

sentences.zh: 至中樞主計請餉必饋常例，天下共知，他幹沒更無算。」

translations.literal: As for the central pivot controlling accounts, requesting pay always required customary gifts — the whole world knows this; other embezzlements are beyond counting."
translations.idiomatic: As for the men at the center who control the accounts, everyone knows that every request for funds carries its customary bribe; their other embezzlements are beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝益心動。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor's mind was moved further.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor was shaken anew.

sentences.zh: 命議舊計臣李待問、傅淑訓，樞臣張國維及戶科荊永祚，兵科沈迅、張嘉言罪，而召縯祚陛見。

translations.literal: He ordered deliberation on the guilt of former accounting ministers Li Daiwen and Fu Shuxun, pivot minister Zhang Guowei, and Revenue Section supervising secretary Jing Yongzuo, War Section Shen Xun and Zhang Jiayan, and summoned Yunzuo for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an inquiry into the former finance ministers Li Daiwen and Fu Shuxun, the pivot minister Zhang Guowei, and the supervising secretaries Jing Yongzuo of the revenue section and Shen Xun and Zhang Jiayan of the war section, and summoned Yunzuo to audience.

sentences.zh: 越數日，抵京。

translations.literal: Several days later he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 又數日入封，召志完、拱乾質前疏中語，拱乾為志完辨，帝頷之。

translations.literal: Several days later he entered audience; Zhwan and Gongqian were summoned to confront the words in the prior memorial; Gongqian defended Zhwan and the emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was received in audience; Zhwan and Gongqian were called to answer the charges in the memorial; Gongqian spoke for Zhwan, and the emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 問縯祚稱功頌德者誰，對曰：「延儒招權納賄，如起廢、清獄、蠲租，皆自居為功。

translations.literal: Asked who was praising merit and extolling virtue, Yunzuo answered: "Yanru monopolizes power and accepts bribes; such things as restoring the dismissed, clearing prisons, and remitting rent — he claims all as his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who had been praising merit and singing virtue, Yunzuo replied: "Yanru hoards power and takes bribes; restoring dismissed officials, clearing the prisons, remitting taxes — he claims every good deed as his own.

sentences.zh: 考選台諫，盡收門下。

translations.literal: In examination selection of censors and remonstrators, he gathers all under his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He packs the censorate and remonstrance offices with his own men.

sentences.zh: 凡求總兵巡撫者，必先賄幕客董廷獻。

translations.literal: All who seek posts as regional commander or grand coordinator must first bribe his secretary Dong Tingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone seeking a command as regional general or provincial governor must first pay off his secretary Dong Tingxian.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，逮廷獻，誅志完，而令縯祚還任。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry, arrested Tingxian, executed Zhwan, and ordered Yunzuo to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage, arrested Tingxian, had Zhwan executed, and sent Yunzuo back to his post.

sentences.zh: 糸寅祚尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Yunzuo soon left office due to bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzuo soon resigned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 福王時，統钅類劾曰廣，因及之，遂逮治。

translations.literal: At the time of Prince Fu, Tong impeached Yueguang and thereby implicated him; he was arrested and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Fu, Tong's impeachment of Yueguang swept Yunzuo in as well, and he was arrested.

sentences.zh: 明年四月與鑣同賜自盡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year he was granted death by suicide together with Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year he and Biao were ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 故事，小臣無賜自盡者。

translations.literal: By precedent, minor officials were not granted death by suicide.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, men of their rank were never granted the privilege of suicide.

sentences.zh: 因良玉兵東下，故大鋮輩急殺之。

translations.literal: Because Liangyu's troops were advancing east, Dacheng and his ilk hurried to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: With Liangyu's army marching east, Dacheng and his allies rushed to dispose of them.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：史可法憫國步多艱，忠義奮發，提兵江滸，以當南北之沖，四鎮棋布，聯絡聲援，力圖興復。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Shi Kefa mourned the nation's difficult steps, roused himself in loyalty and righteousness, led troops on the river banks to meet the north-south juncture, deployed the four garrisons like chess pieces, linked voices and support, and strove to restore.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Shi Kefa grieved the realm's peril, rallied in loyal resolve, took command on the Yangtze to hold the line between north and south, spread the four garrisons like pieces on a board, coordinated their mutual support, and fought to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然而天方降割，權臣掣肘於內，悍將跋扈於外，遂致兵頓餉竭，疆圉曰蹙，孤城不保，志決身殲，亦可悲矣！

translations.literal: Yet Heaven was descending affliction; powerful ministers checked from within, fierce generals acted overbearing without; thus troops stalled, provisions exhausted, borders daily pressed inward; the isolated city could not be preserved; resolve firm, body destroyed — how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven itself seemed bent on ruin: court strongmen hamstrung him from within, unruly generals defied control without, armies stalled and supplies ran dry, the frontier shrank day by day, and the lone city could not stand; he died with his purpose unfulfilled — a tragedy indeed.

sentences.zh: 高弘圖、薑曰廣皆蘊忠謀，協心戮力，而扼于權奸，不安其位。

translations.literal: Gao Hongtu and Jiang Yueguang both harbored loyal designs, united hearts and joined strength, yet were stifled by powerful villains and could not rest in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hongtu and Jiang Yueguang both held loyal designs and worked in concert, yet were blocked by corrupt ministers and driven from office.

sentences.zh: 蓋明祚傾移，固非區區一二人之所能挽也。

translations.literal: For the Ming house's fortune to shift — it was certainly not something one or two men alone could turn back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty's fate was already turning, no handful of men, however devoted, could have reversed it.
